questions.p: Dem dey call African person wey pass school and follow French lifestyle well well as 'évolué'.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the principle of 'Association' introduced by the French later in their colonies?
o: Merging all British and French colonies into a single federal republic
Treating African colonies as equal partners while respecting their local cultures and institutions
Banning all economic activities except agriculture across West Africa
Forcibly deporting all traditional rulers back to Europe for re-education
questions.e: Association was a more pragmatic policy where the French cooperated with local rulers and respected local customs rather than attempting to forcefully turn Africans into French citizens.
questions.p: Association policy mean say French go work with African people and respect their custom instead of forcing everybody to turn French.

questions.q: What was the main consequence of introducing direct taxation into Eastern Nigeria during the colonial era?
o: It caused the complete integration of traditional Islamic laws into customary courts
It resulted in the voluntary resignation of all British colonial governors
It led to the immediate industrialization of the region
It triggered the Aba Women's Riot of 1929 due to fears that women would also be taxed
questions.e: The imposition of direct taxation by Warrant Chiefs sparked intense protests, culminating in the 1929 Aba Women's Riot when women suspected they would be subjected to the same tax.
questions.p: When dem bring tax come East, women vex well well because dem think say dem go tax women too, na im cause the Aba Women Riot of 1929.

questions.q: Under the French colonial administrative setup, what was the status of Africans living in the 'Four Communes' of Senegal?
o: They were granted full French citizenship rights, including the right to vote for a deputy to the French parliament
They were treated strictly as foreign laborers without any rights
They were completely exempted from paying all forms of colonial taxes
They were allowed to practice absolute monarchy free from French laws
questions.e: Residents of the Four Communes (Dakar, Saint-Louis, Rufisque, and Goree) enjoyed special privileges, including French citizenship and voting rights to elect a representative to the French National Assembly.
questions.p: People wey dey live inside the Four Communes for Senegal enjoy better pass others, because dem get French citizenship and fit vote person go French parliament.

questions.q: Which statement correctly contrasts British and French colonial policies in West Africa?
o: The British granted immediate independence to all colonies, while the French maintained them as provinces
The British used traditional rulers through Indirect Rule, while the French practiced Assimilation and central control from Paris
The British centralized all administration in Paris, while the French decentralized through local emirs
The French opposed any form of direct taxation, whereas the British relied solely on communal labor
questions.e: The British favored decentralized rule through native authorities, while the French maintained a centralized policy aimed at turning colonies into overseas extensions of France.
questions.p: British dey use traditional rulers through Indirect Rule, but French dey control everything direct from Paris and want everybody to be like French person.

questions.q: Which of the following organs was central to the execution of Indirect Rule at the local level in Northern Nigeria?
o: The Legislative Council in Lagos
The French National Assembly
The Communal Labour Union
The Native Authority and Native Court system
questions.e: The Native Authority and Native Courts formed the bedrock of the Indirect Rule system, allowing emirs and local councils to collect taxes and maintain law and order under British supervision.
questions.p: Na Native Authority and Native Court dem use make Indirect Rule work well for ground under British supervision.

questions.q: Which of the following bodies was formed in London in 1925 by West African students to foster unity and agitate for political reforms?
o: The West African Students' Union
The National Congress of British West Africa
The People's Union of Lagos
The Nigerian Youth Movement
questions.e: The West African Students' Union (WASU) was established in London in 1925 by Ladipo Solanke and other West African students. It served as a training ground for future nationalist leaders and a platform for anti-colonial agitation.
questions.p: Na West African Students' Union (WASU) dem form for London for 1925 by students like Ladipo Solanke. E help train future leaders and fight against colonial rule.

questions.q: The primary catalyst for the rise of radical nationalism in Nigeria after the Second World War was the
o: introduction of the Clifford Constitution of 1922
economic hardships and the Atlantic Charter's promise of self-determination
establishment of the first indigenous newspaper by Herbert Macaulay
abolition of the slave trade in the British colonies
questions.e: Post-WWII radical nationalism was fueled by severe economic hardships, inflation, unemployment, and the ideals of freedom promoted by the Atlantic Charter which championed self-determination for all people.
questions.p: Na severe economic wahala, high prices, and the promise of self-determination from the Atlantic Charter make people vex well well after World War II to push for independence.

questions.q: The famous Zikist Movement, which advocated militant nationalism and civil disobedience against British rule, derived its name from
o: a secret society formed in the University College Ibadan
the Zaria Province protest of 1948
a traditional deity in Eastern Nigeria
the political philosophy and newspaper of Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe
questions.e: The Zikist Movement was formed in 1946 by young radical admirers of Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe. They took inspiration from his nationalist newspapers and fiery political ideology to demand immediate self-government.
questions.p: Na young boys wey admire Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe form the Zikist Movement for 1946. Dem take style from him newspaper and teaching to fight British people make dem give us independence quick quick.

questions.q: The formation of the National Congress of British West Africa (NCBWA) in 1920 was spearheaded by
o: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa and Aminu Kano
Ernest Ikoli and H. O. Davies
J. E. Casely Hayford and Dr. Akinwande Savage
Obafemi Awolowo and Samuel Akintola
questions.e: The NCBWA was a regional nationalist body founded in 1920 by J. E. Casely Hayford from Gold Coast (Ghana) and Dr. Akinwande Savage from Nigeria to demand elective representation in legislative councils.
questions.p: Na J. E. Casely Hayford from Ghana and Dr. Akinwande Savage from Nigeria join hand form NCBWA for 1920 to ask British make dem allow Africans vote for council.

questions.q: An external factor that greatly accelerated the pace of nationalism in West Africa after 1945 was the
o: defeat of fascism and the emergence of USA and USSR as global superpowers
abolition of the Trans-Atlantic slave trade
signing of the Berlin Conference treaty
discovery of crude oil in commercial quantities
questions.e: The decline of Britain and France as supreme global powers after WWII, coupled with anti-imperialist stances from the USA and USSR, greatly boosted confidence in colonial territories.
questions.p: As World War II finish, Britain and France power reduce, and America and Russia begin support make colonies free. This one make African nationalists get ginger to fight more.

questions.q: Who was the founder and leader of the Egbe Omo Oduduwa, a cultural and socio-political organization that later transformed into the Action Group?
o: Samuel Ladoke Akintola
Ladipo Solanke
Rotimi Williams
Obafemi Awolowo
questions.e: Chief Obafemi Awolowo founded Egbe Omo Oduduwa in London in 1945 as a cultural organization for Yoruba people, which later birthed the Action Group political party in 1951.
questions.p: Na Chief Obafemi Awolowo create Egbe Omo Oduduwa for London for 1945 as Yoruba cultural group, and later na im turn am to Action Group party.

questions.q: The main objective of the Clifford Constitution of 1922 that sparked early nationalist criticism was that
o: it granted total independence to Nigeria
it abolished the amalgamation of Northern and Southern Nigeria
it introduced elective principle only for Lagos and Calabar with strict property qualifications
it made Hausa the official language of administration
questions.e: While the Clifford Constitution introduced the elective principle for the first time in British West Africa, it was heavily criticized because voting was restricted to wealthy males living in Lagos and Calabar who met a high income qualification.
questions.p: Even though Clifford Constitution bring voting system for first time for 1922, nationalists vex because na only rich men wey dey Lagos and Calabar fit vote based on money qualification.

questions.q: Which of the following leaders founded the Northern Elements Progressive Union (NEPU) in 1950 to champion the interests of the talakawa (commoners)?
o: Inuwa Wada
Aminu Kano
Abubakar Tafawa Balewa
Ahmadu Bello
questions.e: Mallam Aminu Kano founded NEPU in August 1950 as a radical political party to challenge the autocratic rule of the traditional northern oligarchy and protect the poor masses.
questions.p: Na Mallam Aminu Kano form NEPU for 1950 to fight for poor people (talakawa) and challenge how traditional rulers dey oppress dem for North.

questions.q: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 replaced which administrative council in Nigeria?
o: The Legislative Council of Lagos Colony only
The West African Court of Appeal
The Northern House of Assembly
The Nigerian Council
questions.e: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 abolished both the Nigerian Council and the old Legislative Council of the Colony of Lagos, replacing them with a single Legislative Council for the colony and southern provinces.
questions.p: Na the Nigerian Council wey Lord Lugard make before, make Clifford Constitution come cancel am for 1922 and put new Legislative Council.

questions.q: Which of the following can be described as a major internal factor that boosted early Nigerian nationalism?
o: The rise of educated African elites and the establishment of local newspapers
The intervention of the United Nations Trusteeship Council
The direct financial funding from the British Crown
The complete absence of ethnic politics in the country
questions.e: The emergence of educated Africans exposed to Western education, coupled with indigenous newspapers, gave citizens the tools to articulate grievances against colonial exploitation.
questions.p: As education grow and people learn book, plus newspapers wey dey talk true, na im open eyes of Nigerians make dem see say colonial rule no good.

questions.q: Which of the following constitutional changes introduced the elective principle into the political history of Nigeria?
o: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951
The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954
The Clifford Constitution of 1922
The Richards Constitution of 1945
questions.e: Sir Hugh Clifford's Constitution of 1922 was the first to introduce the elective principle in Nigeria, allowing a few members to be elected into the Legislative Council from Lagos and Calabar.
questions.p: Na Clifford Constitution of 1922 bring elective principle come Nigeria for the very first time, make people fit vote for Lagos and Calabar.

questions.q: Under which colonial constitution was Nigeria officially divided into three distinct regions: Northern, Western, and Eastern?
o: The Lyttleton Constitution
The Richards Constitution
The Independence Constitution
The Clifford Constitution
questions.e: Sir Arthur Richards formulated the 1945 Constitution (implemented in 1946) which regionalized Nigeria by creating the Northern, Western, and Eastern regions with their own regional councils.
questions.p: Na Richards Constitution wey come out for 1945 divide Nigeria into three major regions: North, West, and East.

questions.q: A major innovation of the Macpherson Constitution of 1951 regarding law-making was the establishment of
o: a fully bicameral federal legislature at Marina
universal adult suffrage throughout the country
regional houses of assembly with legislative powers over specified subjects
the office of the Prime Minister of the Federation
questions.e: The 1951 Macpherson Constitution granted legislative powers to regional houses of assembly for the first time, though subject to the Governor's veto and central review.
questions.p: Na Macpherson Constitution of 1951 give regional houses power to dey make laws for dia own area for the first time.

questions.q: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 is most significant for formally establishing which system of government in Nigeria?
o: Unitary system
Confederal system
Monarchical system
Federal system
questions.e: The 1954 Lyttleton Constitution marked the formal establishment of a true federal structure in Nigeria, clearly demarcating powers between the federal government and the regions.
questions.p: Na Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 make Nigeria become proper federal state, share power well well between federal government and regions.

questions.q: Which Nigerian nationalist fiercely criticized the Richards Constitution of 1945 and led a nationwide tour to protest its provisions?
o: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe
Sir Ahmadu Bello
Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa
Chief Obafemi Awolowo
questions.e: Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe and his party, the NCNC, strongly opposed the Richards Constitution, viewing it as imposed without adequate consultation, and toured Nigeria to raise funds to protest it in London.
questions.p: Na Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe lead him party NCNC to fight Richards Constitution, even travel go London to protest how dem just make am without asking Nigerians.

questions.q: The motion for Nigeria's self-government was moved in the House of Representatives in 1953 by which prominent Nigerian politician?
o: Dr. Michael Okpara
Chief Anthony Enahoro
Mallam Aminu Kano
Chief S. L. Akintola
questions.e: Chief Anthony Enahoro moved the historic motion for self-government in 1953, demanding independence for Nigeria by 1956, which sparked intense political debates.
questions.p: Na Chief Anthony Enahoro move that famous motion for parliament for 1953 make Nigeria gain independence by 1956.

questions.q: What was the primary constitutional consequence of the 1953/1954 London and Lagos Constitutional Conferences?
o: The abolition of the office of the Governor-General
The creation of the Mid-Western Region
The immediate declaration of political independence
The drafting and introduction of the Lyttleton Constitution
questions.e: The constitutional conferences held in London (1953) and Lagos (1954) ironed out disagreements and led directly to the enactment of the Lyttleton Constitution of 1954.
questions.p: Na the meetings wey dem hold for London and Lagos for 1953 and 1954 make dem write the Lyttleton Constitution.

questions.q: Under the Clifford Constitution of 1922, what was the composition of the Legislative Council?
o: An official majority and an unofficial minority
An elected majority and an unofficial minority
An unofficial majority and an official minority
Equal representation of officials and unofficials
questions.e: The 1922 Clifford Constitution provided for an official majority in the Legislative Council, meaning colonial government officials outnumbered the unofficial members, giving ultimate control to the British.
questions.p: Under Clifford Constitution, white people government officials plenty pass Nigerian unofficial members inside the council, so na Oyinbo get final say.

questions.q: Which constitutional milestone provided for the creation of the office of a Governor-General over regional Governors in Nigeria?
o: The Clifford Constitution
The Richards Constitution
The Lyttleton Constitution
The Macpherson Constitution
questions.e: The Lyttleton Constitution elevated the head of the colonial administration from Governor to Governor-General to oversee the newly empowered regional Governors.
questions.p: Na Lyttleton Constitution change the head oga patapata title from Governor to Governor-General to supervise the regional Governors.

questions.q: One major criticism of the Clifford Constitution of 1922 by Nigerian nationalists was that
o: it granted too much autonomy to the regional governments
it denied the Northern provinces representation in the Legislative Council
it abolished all traditional rulers' advisory roles
it introduced universal adult suffrage which confused voters
questions.e: The Clifford Constitution's Legislative Council only legislated for the Southern provinces; the Northern provinces were governed by proclamation of the Governor, excluding them from the central legislative body.
questions.p: Na one major wahala with Clifford Constitution be say na only South members dey inside the council; North no get representation at all at all.

questions.q: The fundamental legal document that granted Nigeria complete sovereignty and freedom from British colonial rule on October 1, 1960, is known as the
o: Macpherson Decree
Amalgamation Instrument
Independence Constitution
Republican Constitution
questions.e: The Independence Constitution of 1960 was the legal instrument that transferred power from Britain to Nigerians, making Nigeria an independent sovereign state within the Commonwealth.
questions.p: Na the Independence Constitution of 1960 be the document wey give Nigeria complete freedom from British people on October 1, 1960.

questions.q: Which of the following constitutions officially severed Nigeria's residual legal ties with the British monarchy by replacing the Governor-General with a Nigerian President?
o: The 1963 Republican Constitution
The 1999 Fourth Republic Constitution
The 1960 Independence Constitution
The 1979 Presidential Constitution
questions.e: The 1963 Constitution transformed Nigeria into a Federal Republic, ending the role of the British monarch as head of state and replacing the Governor-General with a ceremonial President.
questions.p: Na di 1963 Constitution change Naija to Republic, remove British Queen as head of state, and put Nigerian President instead.

questions.q: Under Nigerian federalism, matters such as customs, defence, and external affairs belong exclusively to which legislative list?
o: Emergency legislative list
Exclusive legislative list
Residual legislative list
Concurrent legislative list
questions.e: Items of national importance like defence, foreign policy, and customs are placed on the Exclusive legislative list, meaning only the federal parliament can legislate on them.
questions.p: Matters like army, foreign country wahala, and customs dey inside Exclusive list, na only federal government get power to make laws for dem.

questions.q: In the event of an irreconcilable conflict between a law enacted by a State House of Assembly and a law validly passed by the National Assembly on a matter in the concurrent list, what is the legal position under Nigerian federal constitutions?
o: Both laws become null and void
The state law prevails by virtue of state autonomy
The federal law prevails and the state law becomes void to the extent of its inconsistency
A referendum must be conducted to resolve the conflict
questions.e: The doctrine of federal supremacy applies to the concurrent list; whenever a state law conflicts with a federal law, the federal law prevails while the inconsistent state law is rendered void.
questions.p: If state law and federal law jam for concurrent list, na di federal law go win, and di state law go useless for dat part.

questions.q: Which Nigerian constitution introduced the executive presidential system of government at the federal level, completely separating the executive from the legislature?
o: The 1999 Fourth Republic Constitution
The 1963 Republican Constitution
The 1979 Presidential Constitution
The 1954 Lyttleton Constitution
questions.e: The 1979 Constitution discarded the British-style parliamentary system inherited in 1960 and 1963 and introduced the American-style presidential system.
questions.p: Na di 1979 Constitution carry American style presidential system come Naija, wey separate president from ministers and parliament.

questions.q: Residual powers in Nigerian federalism are constitutionally reserved for which tier of government?
o: Traditional councils
State governments
Local governments
Federal government
questions.e: Residual powers—matters not explicitly mentioned in the exclusive or concurrent lists—are left solely to the state governments under Nigerian federal practice.
questions.p: All those remaining matters wey dem no mention for federal or concurrent list na state government get power over dem.

questions.q: What was a major structural flaw of Nigerian federalism during the Second Republic (1979-1983) regarding state government finances?
o: States were required to fund the federal military budget
States were barred from collecting internal revenue entirely
States collected all oil revenue directly from multinational corporations
States were over-reliant on federally collected revenue distributed through the federation account
questions.e: During the Second Republic, state governments depended overwhelmingly on federally allocated revenue from the federation account, weakening their fiscal autonomy.
questions.p: For Second Republic, state governments over-depend too much on money from federal allocation inside federation account, instead of finding money by themselves.

questions.q: Which body is constitutionally mandated under the 1999 Constitution to handle revenue allocation sharing formulas among the federal, state, and local governments in Nigeria?
o: Federal Inland Revenue Service
Central Bank of Nigeria
Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission
National Planning Commission
questions.e: The Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC) is the statutory body established to monitor and prescribe the revenue-sharing formula among the three tiers of government.
questions.p: Na di Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC) get constitutional power to share money for federal, state, and local government.

questions.q: The fundamental objectives and directive principles of state policy enshrined in the 1979 and 1999 constitutions are legally classified as what?
o: Mandatory criminal codes for citizens
Temporary emergency decrees
Enforceable civil rights in court
Non-justiciable moral and political guidelines for governance
questions.e: Chapter Two of the 1979 and 1999 constitutions contains directive principles which are non-justiciable, meaning citizens cannot sue the government purely for failing to fulfill them.
questions.p: Chapter Two of di constitution talk about good governance, but courts no fit force government to do am because dem non-justiciable.

questions.q: How did the creation of more states in Nigeria over successive military regimes impact the practice of federalism?
o: It completely eliminated the concurrent legislative list
It weakened the federating units and created financial dependence on the central government
It increased fiscal federalism and economic self-sufficiency of local units
It reduced the powers of the federal government and strengthened state autonomy
questions.e: Creating more states fractured the regional power blocs, but it paradoxically increased the financial and political dominance of the central government over smaller, dependent states.
questions.p: As military dey create more states, e scatter regional power, but e come make states dey look up too much to federal government for money.

questions.q: The primary constitutional instrument through which military governments in Nigeria exercised executive and legislative powers was the:
o: Decree
Edict
White Paper
Gazette
questions.e: Military governments at the federal level make laws known as Decrees. Edicts are used by military governors at the state level. White papers and gazettes are official government documents, not primary law-making instruments.
questions.p: Na Decree military government dey use make law for federal level. Edict na for state level, while white paper and gazette just be official government paper.

questions.q: What was the main justification frequently cited by military officers for staging coups d'etat in Nigeria?
o: Widespread corruption, economic mismanagement and electoral malpractice
The desire to hand over power immediately to foreign technocrats
To abolish the federal system of government completely and permanently
The mandate given to them by traditional rulers across the country
questions.e: Nigerian military interventionists almost always justify their actions by pointing to endemic corruption, poor economic performance, and rigged elections by civilian politicians. They present themselves as corrective regimes.
questions.p: Most time, military pipu dey use corruption, bad economy, and rigging of election as excuse to overthrow civilian government. Dem dey yarn say dem come clean up the system.

questions.q: A distinctive structural feature of military administration in Nigeria is the fusion of the:
o: Civil Service and the Traditional Council
Legislature and the Executive
Executive and the Judiciary
Federal and Local Government tiers
questions.e: Under military rule, the Supreme Military Council or Armed Forces Ruling Council exercised both law-making (legislative) and policy-implementing (executive) functions, thereby fusing the two arms of government.
questions.p: Under military rule, law maker and executive work together for one body like Supreme Military Council. Dem dey make law and still dey implement am.

questions.q: The truncation of the Second Nigerian Republic on December 31, 1983, led to the emergence of which military leader as Head of State?
o: General Sani Abacha
General Murtala Muhammed
Major-General Muhammadu Buhari
General Ibrahim Babangida
questions.e: Major-General Muhammadu Buhari took over power from the democratically elected government of President Shehu Shagari on December 31, 1983. He ruled alongside Tunde Idiagbon until August 1985.
questions.p: Na Major-General Muhammadu Buhari overthrow Shehu Shagari government for December 31, 1983. E come rule with Major-General Tunde Idiagbon dat time.

questions.q: The transition program of General Ibrahim Babangida was widely criticized by political analysts primarily because:
o: It suffered from constant shifting of handover dates and political tinkering
It was the shortest transition program in African history
It successfully handed over power without any form of judicial litigation
It strictly adhered to the recommendations of foreign international bodies
questions.e: Babangida's transition program was notoriously characterized by a shifting handover calendar, banning and unbanning of politicians, and the eventual annulment of the June 12, 1993 presidential election.
questions.p: Babangida transition program get too many shifting dates and changing of rules. E come end up with the cancellation of the June 12 election.

questions.q: The policy of 'era of the corrective regime' was first officially popularized in Nigeria by the administration of:
o: Major-General Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi
General Yakubu Gowon
General Murtala Muhammed
General Sani Abacha
questions.e: General Murtala Muhammed's regime, which seized power in July 1975, branded itself as a 'corrective regime' aimed at purging public service corruption, reducing red tape, and correcting the ills of the Gowon administration.
questions.p: Na General Murtala Muhammed government popularize the word 'corrective regime' when dem enter power for 1975 to clean up public service.

questions.q: What major structural change did the Murtala/Obasanjo administration introduce regarding the local government system in Nigeria?
o: It made local governments the fourth tier of government
It abolished local governments and replaced them with development centers
It placed local governments completely under the control of traditional rulers
It established local government as the third tier of government with guaranteed statutory allocations
questions.e: The 1976 Local Government Reforms carried out by the Murtala/Obasanjo regime restructured local government throughout the country and made it the third tier of government, recognizing it with statutory financial allocations.
questions.p: Na the 1976 Local Government reform make local government become the third tier of government wey dey collect money direct from federal allocation.

questions.q: One of the major weaknesses of military rule from a democratic perspective is the absence of:
o: Centralized financial control over the federating units
Accountability, rule of law, and fundamental human rights
Bureaucratic red tape in government ministries
Rapid infrastructural development in urban areas
questions.e: Military regimes operate by decrees and suspension of parts of the constitution, which inherently undermines the rule of law, judicial independence, accountability to citizens, and fundamental human rights.
questions.p: Military rule no get respect for human rights, rule of law, or accountability because dem dey rule by force and decree instead of constitution.

questions.q: The formation of the two political parties, National Republican Convention (NRC) and Social Democratic Party (SDP), was a unique feature of the transition program under:
o: General Muhammadu Buhari
General Ibrahim Babangida
General Abdulsalami Abubakar
General Sani Abacha
questions.e: Under General Ibrahim Babangida, the government created the NRC and SDP as the only two political parties allowed to contest elections, a system famously described as 'a little to the left and a little to the right'.
questions.p: Na General Ibrahim Babangida create NRC and SDP as the only two parties wey Nigerians fit vote for during him transition program.

questions.q: Which of the following is the primary constitutional responsibility of a local government council in Nigeria?
o: Making laws for the peace, order, and good governance of the entire state
Control and regulation of international trade and immigration
Collection of rates, radio and television licences
Formulation of the national monetary and fiscal policies
questions.e: According to the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, local governments are specifically assigned functions such as the collection of rates, radio and television licences, and establishment of markets. The other options are responsibilities of the federal or state governments.
questions.p: Na local government constitutional duty be to collect rates and licences. The other work na federal and state government own.

questions.q: What is the primary rationale for the creation of local governments through the 1976 Local Government Reform in Nigeria?
o: To bring government closer to the grassroots and ensure even development
To serve as a platform for elite political competition
To generate massive revenue exclusively for the federal purse
To completely replace the traditional rulers in community administration
questions.e: The 1976 reform fundamentally restructured local government to be the third tier of government aimed at bringing governance closer to rural communities and accelerating development.
questions.p: Na to bring government nearer to grassroots people and spread development make dem reform local government for 1976.

questions.q: Which organ of a modern Nigerian local government council is responsible for the formulation of bye-laws?
o: The Traditional Council
The Local Government Service Commission
The Executive Committee
The Legislative Council
questions.e: The Legislative Council of a local government, composed of elected councilors from various wards, is empowered to debate and pass bye-laws for the area.
questions.p: Na the legislative council wey consist of elected councillors get power to make bye-laws for local government area.

questions.q: A major challenge confronting local government administration in Nigeria regarding finance is:
o: Inability to spend funds without the approval of the United Nations
Excessive generation of internal revenue making them arrogant
Prohibition from collecting any form of fees or levies
Over-dependence on statutory allocations from the Federation Account
questions.e: Most local governments in Nigeria rely heavily on the Federation Account allocations, making them financially vulnerable whenever oil revenues drop.
questions.p: E dey hard local government because dem too dey depend on money from federation account, so if oil money fall, problem go start.

questions.q: The body responsible for conducting elections into local government councils in a Nigerian state is the:
o: Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)
Revenue Mobilization Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC)
State Independent Electoral Commission (SIEC)
National Orientation Agency (NOA)
questions.e: By law, the State Independent Electoral Commission (SIEC) is empowered to organize, undertake, and supervise all elections into local government councils within the state.
questions.p: Na State Independent Electoral Commission (SIEC) dey conduct election for local government chairman and councillors for state.

questions.q: What was a significant structural defect of the local government system in Nigeria prior to the 1976 nationwide reform?
o: Lack of uniformity, fragmentation, and excessive control by regional or state governments
Absence of traditional rulers in any administrative capacity
Complete autonomy from all forms of government control
Excessive democratization and youth participation
questions.e: Before 1976, local administration varied widely across regions, lacked uniformity, suffered from financial weakness, and was heavily manipulated by regional and state governments.
questions.p: Before 1976 reform, local government system scatter well well, no uniformity, and state government con dey control dem anyhow.

questions.q: Who is the administrative head of the civil service structure in a Nigerian local government council?
o: The Chairman
The Head of Local Government Administration (HOLA)
The Supervisory Councillor
The Commissioner for Local Government Affairs
questions.e: The Head of Local Government Administration (formerly known as the Council Manager or Secretary) is the most senior career civil servant who oversees the day-to-day bureaucracy.
questions.p: Na Head of Local Government Administration (HOLA) be the senior career worker wey dey direct office work and civil servants for council.

questions.q: State control over local governments in Nigeria is legally exercised primarily through the:
o: Federal Ministry of Works
Central Bank of Nigeria
Ministry of Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs
Nigeria Police Force
questions.e: State governments exercise supervisory control over local councils through the State Ministry of Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, which approves budgets and monitors projects.
questions.p: State government dey supervise local government through the Ministry of Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs to make sure things go well.

questions.q: Which of the following constitutes an internal source of revenue for a local government council in Nigeria?
o: Tenement rates, market fees, and motor park tolls
Statutory allocation from the Federation Account
Special grants from foreign donor agencies
Value Added Tax (VAT) shared from the federation pool
questions.e: Internal revenue refers to funds generated locally within the council area, such as tenement rates, market stalls fees, and motor park levies.
questions.p: Internal revenue na the money wey local government generate by themselves like market fees, tenement rates, and motor park money.

questions.q: The concept of 'joint account' between the state and local governments in Nigeria has been criticized mainly because it:
o: Forces local governments to collect taxes directly from foreign countries
Promotes absolute financial autonomy for local councils
Eliminates the need for auditing local government accounts
Allows state governments to allegedly tamper with or withhold local government funds
questions.e: The State-Local Government Joint Account has often been abused by state governors who deduct or withhold statutory allocations meant for grassroots development.
questions.p: Dem criticize State-Local Government Joint Account because state governors dey use am hold or chop money wey suppose go grassroots development.

questions.q: The executive arm of a modern local government council in Nigeria is headed by the:
o: Traditional Ruler
Executive Chairman
Council Leader
Secretary to the State Government
questions.e: The executive arm of the local government is headed by the democratically elected Executive Chairman, alongside the vice-chairman and supervisory councillors.
questions.p: Na the Executive Chairman be head of the executive arm for local government, along side him vice and supervisory councillors.

questions.q: Which historical system of local administration was predominantly utilized by the British colonialists in Northern Nigeria before the introduction of uniform local governments?
o: The Indirect Rule System through Emirs
The Direct Rule System
The General Assembly System
The Communal Administration System
questions.e: The British successfully used the Indirect Rule system in Northern Nigeria, leveraging existing traditional structures and Emirs to administer local affairs.
questions.p: British people use Indirect Rule through Emirs to run local administration for Northern Nigeria before modern local government come enter.

questions.q: Which of the following is widely regarded as the foundational principle and primary center-piece of Nigeria's foreign policy since independence?
o: Unconditional military alliance with Eastern Europe
Africa as the centerpiece of foreign policy
Economic dependency on Western nations
Total eradication of military dictatorships globally
questions.e: Nigeria has consistently placed Africa at the center of its foreign policy since 1960. This principle guides its commitment to decolonization, peace, and integration on the continent.
questions.p: Since Nigeria gain independence, Africa don always be the number one priority for our foreign policy. Na this one make us fight apartheid and support liberation struggles for Africa.

questions.q: The primary objective behind Nigeria's active participation in the peacekeeping operations of ECOMOG in Liberia and Sierra Leone in the 1990s was to
o: secure permanent seats in the United Nations Security Council
expand the territorial boundaries of the Nigerian state
colonize the two war-torn nations for economic gains
restore democratic governance and regional security
questions.e: Nigeria spearheaded ECOMOG to halt the horrific civil wars, stop the massive loss of lives, and restore constitutional order and stability in West Africa.
questions.p: The main reason why Nigeria send soldiers go Liberia and Sierra Leone through ECOMOG na to stop war and bring back peace and democracy to West Africa.

questions.q: Which of the following doctrines was introduced by the administration of General Murtala Muhammed to redefine Nigeria's proactive stance in international affairs?
o: The Concert of Medium Powers
The Geneva Convention
The Murtala Doctrine
The Non-Aligned Doctrine
questions.e: The Murtala Doctrine marked a radical departure from Balewa's conservative foreign policy, making Africa the absolute centerpiece and displaying robust afrocentrism.
questions.p: Na the Murtala Doctrine make Nigeria foreign policy sharp and vibrant, telling the whole world say Africa matters pass anything for our eye.

questions.q: Economic diplomacy, which focused on using international economic relations to attract foreign direct investment and debt relief, was officially introduced by which Nigerian leader?
o: General Yakubu Gowon
General Ibrahim Babangida
General Sani Abacha
Alhaji Shehu Shagari
questions.e: General Ibrahim Babangida's regime introduced economic diplomacy in 1988, championed by External Affairs Minister Ike Omar Nwachukwu, to revamp Nigeria's struggling economy.
questions.p: Na General Ibrahim Babangida introduce economic diplomacy for 1988. The main work na to find foreign investors and help Nigeria reduce debt wahala.

questions.q: Which of the following is a prominent limitation or challenge confronting Nigeria's foreign policy implementation over the years?
o: Overpopulation leading to lack of international relevance
Excessive technological advancement
Total absence of qualified diplomats in the country
Domestic political instability and economic crises
questions.e: Frequent military coups, civil unrest, and fluctuating economic fortunes at home have often weakened Nigeria's financial capacity and moral authority to project power abroad.
questions.p: Internal wahala like military coup, bad economy, and political crisis dey always affect how Nigeria take drive her foreign policy well outside.

questions.q: The concept of 'Concert of Medium Powers', initiated by Nigeria in the late 1980s, was designed to achieve which of the following?
o: Create a mini-Security Council of influential developing nations to dialogue with superpowers
Form a military coalition to invade apartheid South Africa directly
Merge the economies of all West African states into a single currency zone
Boycott the Olympic Games hosted by Western countries
questions.e: Professor Bolaji Akinyemi, as Minister of External Affairs, championed the Concert of Medium Powers to bring together influential middle-power nations to bridge the gap between superpowers and the third world.
questions.p: Professor Bolaji Akinyemi bring the idea of Concert of Medium Powers so that countries wey get moderate power fit join hand talk to superpowers instead of waiting for them.

questions.q: What was the main reason behind Nigeria's decision to boycott the 1986 Commonwealth Games held in Edinburgh, Scotland?
o: Disagreement over the venue selection for the games
A dispute over financial contributions to the Commonwealth secretariat
The outbreak of civil war in Scotland during the event
Britain's refusal to impose economic sanctions on apartheid South Africa
questions.e: Nigeria led a boycott of the 1986 Commonwealth Games because British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher refused to apply economic sanctions against the apartheid government in South Africa.
questions.p: Nigeria tell athletes make them pack their load and refuse to go Commonwealth Games for Scotland for 1986 because Britain refuse to punish apartheid South Africa.

questions.q: Under the First Republic, Nigeria's foreign policy under Prime Minister Abubakar Tafawa Balewa was largely described as
o: radical and aggressively anti-Western
completely isolationist and inward-looking
pro-Western and non-aligned in theory
communist-leaning and pro-Soviet Union
questions.e: Balewa practiced a moderate, pro-Western foreign policy while officially proclaiming a stance of non-alignment during the Cold War era.
questions.p: During First Republic, Abubakar Tafawa Balewa foreign policy dey lean well well towards Western countries, even though dem talk say dem be non-aligned.

questions.q: Which of the following organs of the United Nations is primarily responsible for maintaining international peace and security?
o: The Security Council
The Secretariat
The International Court of Justice
The General Assembly
questions.e: The Security Council holds primary responsibility under the UN Charter for maintaining international peace and security. It has fifteen members, including five permanent members with veto power.
questions.p: Na Security Council get di main power to make sure say peace and safety dey for ground all over di world. Dem get fifteen members, including five wey get veto power.

questions.q: In what year was the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) established through the signing of the Treaty of Lagos?
questions.e: ECOWAS was founded on May 28, 1975, in Lagos, Nigeria, with the signing of the Treaty of Lagos by fifteen West African heads of state to promote economic integration.
questions.p: Dem create ECOWAS for May 28, 1975, for Lagos, Nigeria, when fifteen West African leaders sign di Treaty of Lagos to help business and money matter grow.

questions.q: What is the official headquarters of the African Union (AU)?
o: Abuja, Nigeria
Accra, Ghana
Nairobi, Kenya
Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
questions.e: Addis Ababa, the capital city of Ethiopia, serves as the permanent headquarters and administrative center of the African Union.
questions.p: Na Addis Ababa, wey be di capital city of Ethiopia, dem put di main headquarters and office of di African Union.

questions.q: Which of the following countries is a founding member of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) established in Baghdad in 1960?
o: Angola
Nigeria
Venezuela
Algeria
questions.e: OPEC was founded in Baghdad in September 1960 by five countries: Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and Venezuela. Nigeria joined later in 1971.
questions.p: Na five country start OPEC for Baghdad for 1960, and Venezuela dey among dem. Nigeria come later join for 1971.

questions.q: The Commonwealth of Nations is an association primarily consisting of countries that were formerly part of which empire?
o: The British Empire
The Portuguese Empire
The Belgian Empire
The French Empire
questions.e: The Commonwealth is a voluntary association of independent sovereign states, most of which were former colonies of the British Empire.
questions.p: Commonwealth na association of countries wey independent, and majority of dem na places wey British people been colonize before.

questions.q: Which specialized agency of the United Nations has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, and focuses on international public health?
o: UNICEF
WHO
UNESCO
FAO
questions.e: The World Health Organization (WHO), headquartered in Geneva, is the UN agency responsible for international public health and disease control.
questions.p: Na World Health Organization (WHO) dey charge of health matter all over di world, and dia headquarters dey Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.q: Under the ECOWAS protocol, what major instrument was introduced to facilitate the free movement of persons, right of residence, and establishment within member states?
o: The West African Common Currency
The ECOWAS Protocol on Free Movement
The ECOWAS Brown Card
The Lagos Trade Agreement
questions.e: The ECOWAS Protocol on Free Movement of Persons, Residence and Establishment, adopted in 1979, allows citizens to travel and live within member states without a visa for up to 90 days.
questions.p: Na di ECOWAS Protocol on Free Movement wey dem introduce make citizens fit travel go any member country and stay for up to 90 days without visa.

questions.q: Which organ of the African Union replaces the former Assembly of Heads of State and Government as the supreme policy-making body?
o: The Assembly of the Union
The Pan-African Parliament
The Executive Council
The Peace and Security Council
questions.e: The Assembly of the Union, consisting of all Heads of State and Government of member states, is the supreme policy-making and directing organ of the African Union.
questions.p: Na di Assembly of the Union, wey carry all di presidents and heads of state, stand as di highest body wey dey make law and direct policy for AU.

questions.q: Which of the following countries formally announced its withdrawal from OPEC, taking effect in January 2019?
o: Indonesia
Gabon
Qatar
Ecuador
questions.e: Qatar withdrew from OPEC in January 2019 after nearly 60 years of membership, choosing to focus on natural gas production rather than oil.
questions.p: Qatar commot for OPEC for January 2019 after dem don stay like 60 years, so dat dem go face gas production instead of crude oil.

questions.q: What is the primary criterion for a country to host the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM)?
o: It must be geographically located in Europe
It must have a permanent seat on the UN Security Council
It must be the wealthiest member state
It must volunteer and be chosen by consensus among member states
questions.e: CHOGM is hosted biennially by a voluntary member country whose offer is accepted by consensus among all Commonwealth leaders.
questions.p: Any country wey wan host CHOGM must first volunteer, and all di Commonwealth leaders must agree together before dem go give dem.

questions.q: Which body serves as the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, settling legal disputes submitted by states?
o: The International Criminal Court
The Human Rights Council
The International Court of Justice
The Permanent Court of Arbitration
questions.e: The International Court of Justice (ICJ), located in The Hague, Netherlands, is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations.
questions.p: Na International Court of Justice (ICJ), wey office dey The Hague for Netherlands, be di main court for United Nations to settle matter.

questions.q: What significant structural transformation occurred when the Organization of African Unity (OAU) officially transitioned into the African Union (AU)?
o: It replaced the English language with Swahili as the sole official language.
It dissolved all regional economic communities in Africa.
It merged completely with the European Union administration.
It abandoned the principle of non-interference in internal affairs to allow intervention against war crimes and genocide.
questions.e: Unlike the OAU which strictly upheld non-interference, the AU Constitutive Act grants the Union the right to intervene in a member state in respect of grave circumstances like war crimes and genocide.
questions.p: Unlike OAU wey talk say make nobody put mouth for another country matter, AU constitution allow dem to enter inside country if grave crime like genocide happen.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines 'power' as used in political science?
o: The supreme and final authority of a state over its territory
The ability to compel obedience or influence behaviour, with or without the consent of the people
The right to rule that is accepted and respected by citizens
The moral justification given for occupying a public office
questions.e: Power is simply the capacity to make others act in a certain way, whether they agree or not. This can be through force, influence, or control, unlike authority which needs acceptance.
questions.p: Power na just the fit to make people do wetin you want, whether dem agree or no agree. E fit come from force or control, e no need people gree like authority.

questions.q: Oba Adewale became the traditional ruler of his community strictly according to age-long customs passed down for generations. His subjects obey him mainly because they hold deep respect for these inherited customs and rites. Which type of authority does this scenario best illustrate?
o: Traditional authority
Charismatic authority
Coercive authority
Legal-rational authority
questions.e: Traditional authority is based on long-established customs and practices handed down over time, which people respect and obey. Oba Adewale's authority comes from custom, not from personal charm or written law.
questions.p: Traditional authority na the one wey base on old custom wey don dey since. People dey obey Oba Adewale because of old tradition, no be because of law or because im get special charm.

questions.q: In the fictional state of Edu, the ruling party won an election, but international observers confirmed widespread rigging. Citizens and opposition groups rejected the result and refused to recognise the new government, even though it legally held the instruments of power. This situation best illustrates a government that has:
o: Legal power but lacks legitimacy
Absolute sovereignty but no power
Democratic authority without power
Legitimacy but lacks sovereignty
questions.e: The government controls state machinery (power) and may even be recognised under the law, but because citizens reject its moral right to rule due to rigging, it lacks legitimacy. Legitimacy depends on popular acceptance, not just legal control.
questions.p: The government get the power and even legal backing, but because people no gree say the election dey fair, dem no accept the government as rightful. So dem get power but legitimacy no dey, because legitimacy need people support.

questions.q: Under the Nigerian constitution, even when a political party has a large majority in the National Assembly, it cannot pass laws that strip citizens of fundamental rights such as freedom of speech or fair hearing. This arrangement best demonstrates which democratic principle?
o: Direct democracy
Rule of law and constitutionalism
Tyranny of the majority
Totalitarian rule
questions.e: Rule of law and constitutionalism means that government power, even a majority government, is limited by the constitution and must respect citizens' basic rights. This stops majority rule from becoming oppressive.
questions.p: Rule of law and constitutionalism mean say even if one party get majority for Assembly, the constitution go still limit dia power so dem no fit cheat people out of dia basic rights. E dey protect minority from majority wahala.

questions.q: In many parts of Nigeria, a first-class traditional ruler such as the Emir of a town inherits his position from his royal family rather than through election. This way of choosing a ruler best illustrates which principle of monarchical government?
o: Periodic election
Direct democracy
Rotational leadership
Hereditary succession
questions.e: Monarchy is a system where the position of head of state passes down through a royal bloodline, usually from parent to child. This is called hereditary succession. It is different from systems where leaders are elected or chosen by rotation.
questions.p: Monarchy na system wey leader dey hand over im position to im pikin or family member. Dem no dey vote am, na by blood e dey pass. So na hereditary succession be dat.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key feature that distinguishes a federal system of government from a confederal system?
o: Member units keep separate armies that are not answerable to the centre
The central government depends on the goodwill of member states to survive
The central government gets authority directly from the constitution and the citizens, not from the member units
Member units can withdraw from the union at any time they wish
questions.e: In a federal system, the constitution gives power directly to both the central and state governments, and citizens owe allegiance to both levels. In a confederation, the centre is weak and only exists because member states allow it. This makes a federation more stable and binding than a confederation.
questions.p: For federal system, constitution dey give power direct to both central and state government, and di citizens dey under both. But for confederation, di centre weak and e dey depend on wetin di states agree. Na dat one make federal system strong pass confederation.

questions.q: A unitary system of government is usually adopted by a country mainly because it wants to achieve which of the following?
o: A free right for any region to secede whenever it wishes
Strong regional governments with their own independent constitutions
Multiple centres of sovereign power sharing authority equally
Uniform laws and policies applied equally across the whole country
questions.e: A unitary system concentrates power at the centre, which makes it easier to apply the same laws and policies to every part of the country. This is different from federalism, which allows regional differences, or confederalism, which allows states to keep strong independence.
questions.p: Unitary system dey put power for one centre, so dem fit make one kind law and policy wey go dey apply for everywhere for di kontri. Na dat one make am different from federal or confederal system wey dey allow states get plenty independent power.

questions.q: Three neighbouring kingdoms decide to form a loose union. Each kingdom keeps its own army, its own laws, and can leave the union at any time it chooses. A small joint secretariat only helps them coordinate trade matters between themselves. Which form of government does this arrangement best describe?
o: Confederation
Unitary state
Federation
Constitutional monarchy
questions.e: A confederation is a loose association where member states keep full sovereignty, control their own armies and laws, and can withdraw freely, while the central body is weak and only handles limited shared matters. This is different from a federation, where the centre has strong constitutional powers over member states and withdrawal is not easy.
questions.p: Confederation na when di small states still hold their full power, dem get their own army and law, and dem fit comot anytime dem like, while di centre dey weak and e dey only handle small common matter like trade. Dis one different from federation wey di centre strong well well and states no fit just waka comot.

questions.q: In a modern democratic state, which arm of government is primarily saddled with the responsibility of carrying out and enforcing the laws made by the legislature?
o: The Judiciary
The Civil Service Commission
The Executive
The Legislature
questions.e: The executive arm, headed by the President or Governor and the ministries/agencies under it, is responsible for implementing and enforcing laws. The legislature makes laws while the judiciary interprets them.
questions.p: Na Executive dey carry out and enforce di laws wey Legislature don make. Legislature na im dey make law, Judiciary na im dey interpret am.

questions.q: Under the Nigerian presidential system, if the President withholds assent to a bill passed by the National Assembly, the bill can still become law if the National Assembly does which of the following?
o: Asks the Vice President to sign the bill instead
Passes the bill again with a two-thirds majority vote in each chamber
Submits the bill to the state Houses of Assembly for ratification
Sends the bill directly to the Supreme Court for approval
questions.e: This is a classic check on executive power: if the President refuses to sign a bill, the National Assembly can override the veto by repassing it with a two-thirds majority in both the Senate and House of Representatives. This makes the bill law without presidential assent.
questions.p: If President no gree sign bill, National Assembly fit override am if dem pass di bill again with two-third majority for both Senate and House of Reps. Na dis one go make di bill become law even without President signature.

questions.q: Which constitutional power enables a State House of Assembly to remove a sitting Governor from office before the end of his tenure, where he is found guilty of gross misconduct?
o: Judicial review
Veto
Impeachment
Dissolution
questions.e: Impeachment is the legislative process by which a State House of Assembly can remove a Governor found guilty of gross misconduct, following constitutional procedures. This is a key check on the executive by the legislature.
questions.p: Impeachment na di process wey State House of Assembly dey use remove Governor wey dem find guilty of serious misconduct. Na im be check wey Legislature get on Executive.

questions.q: In a certain country, the same body makes the laws, directly enforces them through its own agents, and also sits to judge disputes arising from those laws, without any separate institution checking it. This arrangement most clearly violates which principle of government?
o: Rule of law
Separation of powers
Federalism
Fundamental human rights
questions.e: Separation of powers requires that lawmaking, law enforcement, and adjudication be handled by three distinct, independent arms (legislature, executive, judiciary). When one body performs all three functions without checks, this concentration of power directly violates the doctrine of separation of powers.
questions.p: Separation of powers mean say three different arms (Legislature, Executive, Judiciary) suppose dey handle law-making, enforcement and judgment separately. If one body dey do everything alone without check, e don break dis principle well well.

questions.q: Which type of constitution is best described as one in which independent states come together to form a loose union, each retaining its own sovereignty, and the central authority only handles matters specifically agreed upon such as defence or foreign affairs?
o: Monarchical constitution
Federal constitution
Unitary constitution
Confederal constitution
questions.e: A confederal constitution joins sovereign states loosely, with the centre having only limited, agreed powers while member states keep most of their independence. This differs from a federal system where power is shared constitutionally between a strong centre and states, and from a unitary system where power is concentrated at the centre.
questions.p: Confederal constitution na when different independent states join together loosely, but each one still get im own power. Di central body na small-small matter dem dey handle, like defence. E different from federal (wia centre and states share power by law) and unitary (wia centre get all di power).

questions.q: In constitutional law, when courts interpret the constitution and their rulings on its meaning are later relied upon as guides in similar cases, this source of the constitution is called
o: Judicial precedents
Conventions
Customs and traditions
Religious doctrines
questions.e: Judicial precedents arise when courts give authoritative interpretations of constitutional provisions, and these decisions guide how the same provisions are understood and applied in future cases. This is different from conventions, which are unwritten customary practices in government, not court rulings.
questions.p: Judicial precedent na wen court interpret constitution and dat ruling later become guide for similar cases wey go come. E no be convention, wey be unwritten custom wey government dey follow; na court decision we dey talk about here.

questions.q: A provision in a constitution that can only be changed through a special, more difficult procedure (such as a two-thirds majority vote plus a national referendum) rather than by ordinary legislative process is known as a/an
o: Preambular clause
Entrenched clause
Residual clause
Delegated clause
questions.e: An entrenched clause is specially protected so that it cannot be amended as easily as ordinary laws; it requires extra steps like a supermajority or referendum. This protects important provisions, such as fundamental human rights, from being changed carelessly by a simple parliamentary majority.
questions.p: Entrenched clause na part of constitution wey dem protect well-well, so dem no fit just change am like ordinary law. To change am, dem need special process like two-thirds majority plus referendum, so dat important matters no go dey change anyhow.

questions.q: Country Alpha's constitution can be changed whenever the National Assembly passes an ordinary bill by simple majority, just like any other law. Country Beta's constitution requires a two-thirds majority in the legislature plus approval by a national referendum before any amendment takes effect. Based on this information, how should these two constitutions be classified?
o: Alpha is rigid, Beta is flexible
Alpha is flexible, Beta is rigid
Both are rigid because they are both written
Both are flexible because they both allow amendment
questions.e: A constitution is classified as flexible or rigid based on how difficult it is to amend, not merely whether it is written. Alpha is flexible because it can be changed by ordinary simple-majority legislation, while Beta is rigid because it demands a special, harder procedure (supermajority plus referendum) before any change can occur.
questions.p: Wetin dey make constitution rigid or flexible na how hard e be to change am, no be say e dey written or not. Alpha dey flexible because ordinary simple majority fit change am, but Beta dey rigid because e need special wahala like two-thirds majority and referendum before e go change.

questions.q: Which of the following fundamental rights guaranteed under Chapter IV of the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria (as amended) CANNOT be suspended or taken away even during a declared state of emergency?
o: Right to freedom of association
Right to freedom of expression and the press
Right to freedom of movement
Right to the dignity of the human person
questions.e: The right to dignity of the human person (freedom from torture and inhuman treatment) is a non-derogable right; it stays protected no matter the circumstance. Rights like movement, expression and association can be lawfully restricted during emergencies for public safety.
questions.p: Right to dignity of human person (no torture, no inhuman treatment) na right wey dem no fit remove at all, even for emergency time. But freedom of movement, expression and association fit dey limited small during emergency for safety reasons.

questions.q: Chief Okafor was arrested by the police in Enugu and kept in detention for three weeks without being charged before any court, even though the Constitution requires that a suspect be brought to court within a reasonable time. Which principle of the rule of law has been breached in this situation?
o: Equality of all citizens regardless of social status
Separation of powers between the three arms of government
Protection of personal liberty through due process of law
Supremacy of customary law over statutory law
questions.e: The rule of law demands that a person's liberty can only be taken away through due legal process, including timely arraignment in court. Holding Chief Okafor for three weeks without charge violates this protection of personal liberty, not the other listed principles.
questions.p: Rule of law talk say dem fit only take person liberty if dem follow correct legal process, like to charge am to court on time. Since dem hold Chief Okafor pass three weeks without charge, na the protection of personal liberty dem break, no be the other ones.

questions.q: Under the principle of equality before the law in a democracy, every citizen is ordinarily expected to be subject to the same legal process. However, the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria grants one category of public officer a temporary immunity from civil and criminal proceedings while serving in office. Which officer enjoys this immunity?
o: A serving State Governor
The Senate President
The Inspector-General of Police
The Chief Justice of Nigeria
questions.e: Section 308 of the 1999 Constitution grants immunity from legal proceedings to the President, Vice President, Governors and Deputy Governors while they remain in office. The Senate President, IGP and Chief Justice do not enjoy this special constitutional immunity.
questions.p: Section 308 of di Constitution give immunity from court case to President, Vice President, Governors and Deputy Governors as dem dey office. Senate President, IGP and Chief Justice no get dis kain special immunity.

questions.q: Suppose the National Assembly passes an Act that directly conflicts with the fundamental rights provisions contained in Chapter IV of the 1999 Constitution. Based on the rule of law principle of constitutional supremacy, what is the likely legal outcome for that Act?
o: The Act overrides the Constitution because the Assembly represents the people
The Act becomes automatically void to the extent of its inconsistency with the Constitution
The Act can only take effect after the President personally approves it
The Act remains fully valid until the same Assembly chooses to repeal it
questions.e: Section 1(3) of the 1999 Constitution states that any law inconsistent with the Constitution is void to the extent of the inconsistency, because the Constitution is supreme over every other law, including Acts of the National Assembly. This reflects the rule of law idea that no law-making body is above the Constitution.
questions.p: Section 1(3) of di Constitution talk say any law wey no match wit di Constitution na im go cancel for di part wey clash, becos Constitution na di highest law pass any Act. Dis one show say even National Assembly no fit pass law wey go pass di Constitution.

questions.q: Which of the following is a basic feature that distinguishes a political party from a pressure group in a democratic system like Nigeria's?
o: A political party sponsors and fields candidates for elective office, while a pressure group does not contest elections
A political party must be older than any pressure group before it can operate
A political party always has more members than a pressure group
A political party can only operate in urban centres, unlike pressure groups
questions.e: The key difference is that political parties aim to win political power by presenting candidates for election, while pressure groups only try to influence government decisions without contesting elections. Age, size and location are not the defining features.
questions.p: The main difference na say political party dey bring candidates to contest election, but pressure group no dey contest election, dem just dey influence government. Age, number of members or where dem dey operate no be the real difference.

questions.q: In a dominant-party system, which of the following best describes the political situation in that country?
o: No political party is allowed to exist, and the military rules directly
All political parties are compulsorily merged into a single ruling party by law
Two parties exist and alternate in winning power with almost equal strength
Several political parties legally exist, but one party keeps winning elections and controlling government for a long stretch of time
questions.e: A dominant-party system allows many parties to exist and compete, but one party consistently wins elections and remains in power for a long period due to its strong organisation or popularity. This differs from a one-party state where other parties are banned by law.
questions.p: For dominant-party system, plenty parties dey, dem fit contest election, but one particular party dey always win and dey stay for power for long time because dem strong well well. E different from one-party state wey ban other parties by law.

questions.q: A pressure group in Nigeria decides to challenge a new government policy by filing a case in court instead of organizing street protests or lobbying lawmakers directly. Which method of pressure group action is this group using?
o: Mass media propaganda and advertisement campaigns
Direct sponsorship of candidates for election
Judicial action through litigation in the law courts
Industrial strike action by withdrawing labour
questions.e: When a pressure group goes to court to challenge a government policy, it is using the judicial method, also called litigation, to achieve its aim. This is different from striking, media campaigns or sponsoring candidates, which are other separate methods.
questions.p: When pressure group carry case go court to challenge government policy, na judicial method or litigation dem dey use. E different from strike, media campaign or sponsoring candidate, wey be other different methods.

questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria (as amended), how is the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) appointed?
o: By the Council of State without further confirmation
By the Chief Justice of Nigeria on behalf of the judiciary
By the President, subject to confirmation by the Senate
By the National Assembly through a special resolution
questions.e: The Constitution gives the President power to appoint the INEC Chairman, but this appointment only becomes valid after the Senate confirms it. This is meant to prevent the President from acting alone on such an important office.
questions.p: Di Constitution give Oga President power to appoint INEC Chairman, but e no fit final until Senate confam am. Dis one dey make sure say President no go just dey appoint anybody anyhow.

questions.q: During a local government election in Oyo State, agents of a candidate were caught giving out cash of ₦2,000 to voters right before they entered the polling unit, on condition that they vote for their candidate. This act is best described as
o: Vote buying
Political apathy
Gerrymandering
Ballot stuffing
questions.e: Vote buying is when money or gifts are offered to voters to influence how they cast their vote. Gerrymandering is about manipulating constituency boundaries, ballot stuffing is illegally adding extra ballots, and apathy means lack of interest in voting, so none of these fit the scenario.
questions.p: Na vote buying be dis one, because dem give voters money make dem vote one candidate. Gerrymandering na about boundary wahala, ballot stuffing na when dem add fake ballot paper, and apathy na when people no wan vote at all, so dem no fit be di answer.

questions.q: In a single-member constituency election using the First-Past-The-Post (simple plurality) system, three candidates contested as follows: Ade scored 42% of total votes, Bola scored 33%, and Chika scored 25%. According to this electoral system, who wins the seat?
o: Bola, because the two lowest scorers' votes should be added to decide a run-off
Ade, because he has the highest number of votes even though it is not up to 50%
Chika, because minority candidates are protected under this system
No one, because a winner must score above 50% of total votes
questions.e: Under First-Past-The-Post, the candidate with the single highest number of votes wins the seat, even if that number is less than half of all votes cast; there is no requirement for an outright majority or a run-off. This is different from systems that demand 50% plus one vote to win.
questions.p: For First-Past-The-Post system, na di candidate wey get di highest votes dey win, even if di votes no reach 50%. Dis system no need person score pass half of di total votes before e fit win, so Ade don win based on say e get di most votes.

questions.q: Which term best describes the legal status that confers on a person full rights, privileges and duties as a recognised member of a sovereign state?
o: Statelessness
Domicile
Naturalization
Citizenship
questions.e: Citizenship is the legal status that gives a person full rights (like voting) and duties (like paying tax) as a recognised member of a state. Domicile just means where one lives, naturalization is a process of becoming a citizen, and statelessness means having no citizenship at all.
questions.p: Citizenship na di legal status wey give person full rights (like to vote) and duties (like to pay tax) as member of one country. Domicile na just where person dey stay, naturalization na di process to become citizen, and statelessness mean say person no get any citizenship at all.

questions.q: A group of students in Kaduna State is asked to list factors that usually shape public opinion in a democratic society. Which of the following items does NOT belong to that list?
o: Religious beliefs
Personal height of citizens
Level of education
Mass media reportage
questions.e: Public opinion is shaped by things like education, religion, and the media because these affect how people think about issues. A person's physical height has nothing to do with how they form opinions on public matters.
questions.p: Public opinion dey shape by education, religion and media because dis ones dey affect how people dey think about matter. But person height no get anything to do with how dem dey form opinion on public issue.

questions.q: In two neighbouring villages, Umuahia A and Umuahia B, the children grow up with different political attitudes because one village has mission schools that stress civic duty while the other relies mainly on traditional elders' teachings. This difference in political attitudes between the two villages is best explained by the concept of:
o: Electoral behaviour
Public opinion
Political socialisation
Citizenship education
questions.e: Political socialisation is the lifelong process by which people learn political values and attitudes from agents like schools, family, and elders. The different agents (mission schools versus elders) in the two villages explain why the children develop different political orientations.
questions.p: Political socialisation na di process wey person dey learn political values from agents like school, family and elders. Because di two villages get different agents (mission school versus elders), na why di pikin dem get different political attitude.

questions.q: A Lagos-based magazine claims that 80% of Nigerians support a new tax policy, but the survey was conducted only among wealthy businesspeople in Victoria Island. A trained analyst would say this result is unreliable mainly because of:
o: Political apathy
Censorship
Propaganda
Sampling bias
questions.e: Sampling bias happens when a survey only questions a narrow, unrepresentative group instead of a cross-section of the whole population, making the result inaccurate. Here, wealthy Victoria Island businesspeople cannot represent the views of all Nigerians, so the 80% figure is misleading.
questions.p: Sampling bias na when survey only ask small group wey no represent everybody, so di result no go correct. Since na only rich Victoria Island business people dem ask, di 80% figure no fit show wetin all Nigerians think.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the civil service in Nigeria?
o: The body of permanent, paid officials who implement government policies in ministries and departments
The elected members of the National Assembly who make laws for the federation
The group of political appointees who determine government policies
The judicial officers who interpret laws in the law courts
questions.e: The civil service consists of permanent, salaried officials who carry out government policies but do not make them. Legislators, political appointees and judges belong to other arms or categories of government, not the civil service.
questions.p: Civil service na di permanent workers wey dey collect salary and dey carry out government policies, dem no dey make di policies. Legislators, political appointees and judges na different category entirely, no be civil service.

questions.q: Which of the following best distinguishes the civil service from the wider public service in Nigeria?
o: Civil service workers earn higher salaries than all other public service workers
The civil service is elected while the public service is appointed
The civil service covers only workers in core government ministries and departments, while the public service also includes employees of public corporations, the judiciary and the armed forces
The civil service exists only at state level while the public service exists only at federal level
questions.e: The civil service is a narrower term referring to officials in ministries, departments and agencies that carry out routine administration. The public service is broader, covering these plus workers in public corporations, courts, the military and police.
questions.p: Civil service na di small part wey be ministries and departments workers wey dey do normal admin work. Public service na di big umbrella wey cover civil service plus public corporations, courts, military and police workers.
