questions.q: A government ministry depends almost entirely on yearly budget allocation from the Ministry of Finance to run its activities. A public corporation that supplies water to a city, however, gets part of its money from selling water to customers in addition to government subvention, and it has its own legal identity separate from the ministry. Based on this situation, which statement best explains why public corporations enjoy greater operational autonomy than ordinary ministries?
o: Public corporations can generate part of their revenue internally and, having separate legal personality, can enter contracts and manage funds with less day-to-day ministerial control
Public corporations are not required to render account to any government body since they generate their own funds
Public corporations receive no funding at all from government and operate exactly like private companies
Public corporations are exempted from all government policies because they are privately owned
questions.e: Because a corporation has its own legal personality and can earn internal revenue, it can sign contracts and manage its budget with less direct ministerial interference than a ministry that relies solely on treasury funds. It still remains accountable to government through its supervising ministry and audits.
questions.p: Since corporation get im own legal personality and dey make money from wetin e dey sell, e fit sign contract and manage im money without too much ministry control. E still dey answerable to government through im supervising ministry and audit, no be say e free complete.

questions.q: In the pre-colonial Hausa-Fulani political system, which title was held by the chief military commander who led the emir's army into battle?
o: Waziri
Madawaki
Galadima
Sarkin Fada
questions.e: The Madawaki was the title of the chief military commander in the Hausa-Fulani system, responsible for leading the emir's army in war. The Waziri was the chief adviser, the Galadima often administered the capital, and the Sarkin Fada supervised the palace.
questions.p: Madawaki na the title wey dem give the army commander wey dey lead the emir soja go war. Waziri na the main adviser, Galadima dey manage capital, Sarkin Fada dey oversee palace matters.

questions.q: In the old Oyo Empire, the Oyo Mesi was a council of principal chiefs, headed by the Bashorun, that could check the Alaafin's power. How many principal chiefs made up this council?
o: Five
Twelve
Nine
Seven
questions.e: The Oyo Mesi was made up of seven principal chiefs, led by the Bashorun, who advised the Alaafin and could also check his excesses. This number is a well-established fact about Oyo Empire administration.
questions.p: Oyo Mesi na council of seven big chiefs, Bashorun dey lead dem, and dem get power to advise and even check Alaafin if e dey misbehave. Na seven chiefs dem dey use for dis council.

questions.q: In pre-colonial Igbo society, which institution allowed a wealthy and respected man to gain political and social influence by paying for an expensive, prestigious title?
o: Ozo title society
Age-grade system
Osu caste practice
Umuada association
questions.e: The Ozo title society was an institution in Igbo land where a man of means could pay to take a prestigious title, which raised his social status and gave him political influence in the community. Age-grades organised people by age for communal duties, Umuada was for married daughters of the lineage, and Osu referred to an outcast class, not a title system.
questions.p: Ozo title society na where rich and respected man go pay money take important title, wey go give am status and political power for im community. Age-grade na people wey dem group by age for work, Umuada na married daughters group, Osu na outcast class, no be title society.

questions.q: Under British colonial policy in Africa, which statement best defines the system known as Indirect Rule?
o: Direct administration of colonies by European officials without any local involvement
Governing the people through existing traditional rulers who worked under the supervision of colonial officials
Complete military occupation with no form of local administration at all
Granting full citizenship and voting rights of the colonial power to all Africans
questions.e: Indirect Rule meant the British ruled through traditional chiefs and emirs, who took orders from colonial Residents. This saved money and manpower while still keeping real control in British hands.
questions.p: Indirect Rule na where British dey rule through native chiefs and emirs, but dem dey report to British Residents. E dey save British money and workers, but British still dey hold the real power.

questions.q: Lord Lugard chose to model Indirect Rule in Northern Nigeria on an existing political structure because it already had organised chiefs, courts and tax systems. Which structure was this?
o: The Igbo village council system
The Benin palace guild system
The Sokoto Caliphate emirate system
The Yoruba obaship confederacy
questions.e: The Sokoto Caliphate already had emirs, Islamic courts and an organised tax (zakat/jangali) system before the British arrived. Lugard simply placed British Residents above the emirs instead of creating a new system from scratch.
questions.p: Sokoto Caliphate already get emirs, courts and tax system before British come. Lugard just put British Resident on top of the emirs instead of starting new system.

questions.q: Unlike the British, the French ran their West African colonies as a highly centralised and direct system of administration. This means that:
o: African traditional kingdoms kept full independent authority over their territories
Local rulers in French colonies could make laws without approval from Paris
French colonies used the same House of Chiefs arrangement as the British colonies
All real administrative power flowed from Paris through appointed French officials, with African chiefs acting only as agents carrying out orders
questions.e: French policy treated colonies as extensions of France itself, so power was centralised in Paris and passed down through Governors-General to French-appointed chiefs. These chiefs had no independent authority like emirs under British Indirect Rule; they simply executed French orders.
questions.p: French dey see their colonies as part of France, so power dey come from Paris through French Governor to the chiefs wey dem appoint. Dis chiefs no get independent power like emirs for British system; dem just dey carry out French orders.

questions.q: Because Eastern Nigeria lacked large centralised kingdoms like those in the North, the British created a new class of local government agents to help collect tax and keep order. These agents were called:
o: Warrant Chiefs
District Officers
Residents
Emirs
questions.e: Since many Eastern communities were organised in small, independent village groups rather than centralised kingdoms, the British appointed local men and gave them a 'warrant' of authority to act as chiefs, even where such a position never existed before. These became known as Warrant Chiefs.
questions.p: For Eastern Nigeria, plenty communities no get big central kingdom like North. So British go appoint some men, give dem 'warrant' make dem act as chief, even though such position no dey before. Na dem be Warrant Chiefs.

questions.q: Which newspaper, founded by Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe in 1937, became one of the most powerful tools for spreading nationalist ideas and criticising colonial rule across Nigeria?
o: Daily Times
Nigerian Tribune
The Comet
West African Pilot
questions.e: The West African Pilot, established by Azikiwe in 1937, used bold articles to awaken political awareness and attack colonial policies. It became a major voice for nationalist agitation before independence.
questions.p: Na West African Pilot, wey Azikiwe start am for 1937, dem dey use spread nationalist ideas and dey talk against colonial rule. E be like strong mouthpiece wey many Nigerians dey read.

questions.q: The National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC), formed in 1944, was set up mainly to
o: serve purely as a trade union for railway workers
unite Nigerians and Cameroonians in a broad-based nationalist movement against colonial policies
promote exclusively cultural festivals among the Igbo people
create a single political party meant only for Northern Nigeria
questions.e: The NCNC brought together various Nigerian and Cameroonian groups to form a strong, nationwide movement demanding greater political participation and an end to colonial domination. It was not limited to one region or ethnic group.
questions.p: Dem form NCNC for 1944 to bring Nigerians and Cameroonians togeda so dem fit fight colonial rule as one big group. E no be only for one region or one tribe.

questions.q: A major reason Nigerian nationalists strongly criticised the Richards Constitution of 1946 was that it
o: abolished all native courts across the country
removed British officials completely from the Legislative Council
introduced regionalism and major constitutional changes without adequate consultation with Nigerian leaders
granted Nigeria full self-government ahead of schedule
questions.e: Nigerian leaders were angry that Governor Richards introduced far-reaching changes, including dividing Nigeria into three regions, without proper consultation with them. This lack of consultation fuelled nationalist protests and demands for more Nigerian involvement in governance.
questions.p: Richards Constitution bring regionalism and big changes but e no first ask Nigerian leaders well well. Na dis kind one-sided decision make nationalists vex and dey agitate for better involvement.

questions.q: After the Second World War, many Nigerian ex-servicemen who had fought for Britain returned home to face unemployment and racial discrimination despite their wartime sacrifices. How did this situation mainly affect Nigerian nationalism?
o: It pushed many ex-servicemen to join and strengthen the agitation for self-rule and fair treatment
It caused the ex-servicemen to form a new colonial police force loyal to Britain
It made the ex-servicemen migrate permanently to Britain to seek better treatment
It made the colonial government immediately grant independence to avoid unrest
questions.e: Having fought and suffered for Britain, the ex-servicemen expected fair treatment and reward at home. Instead they faced neglect, so they joined nationalist movements, bringing discipline, organisation and urgency to the independence struggle.
questions.p: Dem soldiers wey fight for Britain come back meet no job and bad treatment for dia own country. Dat kain disappointment push many of dem to join nationalist struggle well well, add strong organisation give am.

questions.q: The Richards Constitution of 1945 is chiefly remembered in Nigeria's constitutional history for introducing which feature?
o: Internal self-government for all three regions at the same time
A full federal system with regional premiers and cabinets
The principle of regionalism by grouping Nigeria into three regions for legislative discussion
Direct election of members into the Legislative Council by the people
questions.e: Richards' main contribution was dividing Nigeria into Northern, Western and Eastern regions, each with its own House for discussing bills before they went to the central Legislative Council. Direct elections, premiers and self-government came much later under other constitutions.
questions.p: Richards Constitution main work na to divide Nigeria into three regions wey go dey discuss bills before dem reach central council. Election by all people, premiers and self-government come later under other constitutions.

questions.q: By the end of the 1957 Constitutional Conference, which two regions of Nigeria had been granted internal self-government ahead of the North?
o: Eastern and Northern regions
Western region alone, with no other region granted self-government
Northern and Western regions
Western and Eastern regions
questions.e: The Western and Eastern Regions achieved internal self-government in 1957 because their leaders pushed strongly for early self-rule. The Northern Region, due to concerns about readiness in education and administration, delayed and only got internal self-government in 1959.
questions.p: Western and Eastern Region get internal self-government for 1957 because dia leaders push hard for am. Northern Region fear say dem no ready well-well for education and administration, so dem get their own self-government for 1959.

questions.q: During the constitutional talks leading to Nigeria's independence, Northern Region leaders were initially reluctant to accept an early self-government date (such as 1956) proposed by some Southern politicians. What was the main reason for this reluctance?
o: They preferred that the British continue to rule Nigeria indefinitely without any change
They feared the North lagged behind in Western education and trained manpower needed to run a modern government
They wanted the North to break away completely and form a separate country
They insisted that the federal capital be relocated from Lagos to the North before any self-government talks
questions.e: Northern leaders, aware that Western education and the civil service had developed more in the South, worried that early self-government would let Southern-trained Nigerians dominate a united Nigeria. This made them push for a slower, phased approach rather than outright secession or permanent colonial rule.
questions.p: Northern leaders sabi say Western education and civil service dey more for South, so dem fear say South go dominate if self-government come too fast. Na why dem want slow slow process, no be say dem wan break away or make British stay forever.

questions.q: Under the 1963 Republican Constitution, who became Nigeria's Head of State, replacing the British monarch who had been represented by a Governor-General?
o: President
Premier
Prime Minister
Governor
questions.e: The 1963 Constitution made Nigeria a republic, so the Queen was replaced by a Nigerian President as Head of State. The Prime Minister remained Head of Government, while Premiers headed the regions.
questions.p: 1963 Constitution turn Nigeria to republic, so Nigerian President take over as Head of State instead of di Queen. Prime Minister still dey as Head of Government, Premiers dey lead di regions.

questions.q: Which of the following matters falls under the Concurrent Legislative List in the 1999 Constitution, meaning both the National Assembly and a State House of Assembly can validly make laws on it?
o: External affairs
Electricity generation and distribution
Currency and coinage
Immigration
questions.e: Electricity generation and distribution is on the Concurrent List, so both federal and state legislatures can make laws on it, though federal law prevails if there is a conflict. Currency, external affairs and immigration are strictly on the Exclusive List for the federal government alone.
questions.p: Electricity generation and distribution dey for Concurrent List, so both National Assembly and State Assembly fit make law on top am, but federal law go win if clash happen. Currency, external affairs and immigration na only federal government fit touch dem, dem dey Exclusive List.

questions.q: The federal character principle, first entrenched in the 1979 Constitution and retained in the 1999 Constitution, was mainly introduced to achieve which of the following?
o: Direct election of traditional rulers into the Senate
Automatic creation of more states to balance population figures
Fair representation of Nigeria's various ethnic and state groups in government appointments
Equal distribution of mineral resources among the states
questions.e: The federal character principle requires that appointments to federal institutions reflect the diversity of Nigeria's states and ethnic groups, preventing domination by any single group. It is about representation in government, not resource sharing, state creation, or electing traditional rulers.
questions.p: Federal character principle mean say wen dem dey appoint people for federal jobs, dem must carry all states and ethnic groups follow, so one group no go dominate. E no concern resource sharing, state creation, or election of traditional rulers.

questions.q: At independence in 1960, Nigeria was a federation of three regions - Northern, Eastern and Western. Which additional region was created shortly before the 1963 Republican Constitution took effect, bringing the total number of regions to four?
o: Niger Delta Region
Benue Region
North-Central Region
Mid-Western Region
questions.e: The Mid-Western Region was carved out of the former Western Region in 1963, making Nigeria a four-region federation just before the Republican Constitution came into force. The other options are not regions that existed at that time.
questions.p: Dem carve Mid-Western Region comot from di old Western Region for 1963, so Nigeria become four-region federation before di Republican Constitution start. Di oda options no be regions wey dey exist dat time.

questions.q: Who became Nigeria's first military Head of State, following the coup d'etat of January 1966?
o: Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi
Sani Abacha
Yakubu Gowon
Murtala Mohammed
questions.e: After the January 1966 coup, Major-General Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi took over as Head of State, making him Nigeria's first military ruler. Gowon took over later that same year after a counter-coup.
questions.p: After di January 1966 coup, Major-General Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi take over as Head of State, so na him be di first military ruler for Nigeria. Gowon come take over later dat same year afta counter-coup.

questions.q: Under military administrations in Nigeria, the body that served as the highest policy-making organ, usually made up of the Head of State and senior military officers, was called the:
o: National Council of Ministers
Council of State
Supreme Military Council
Federal Executive Council
questions.e: The Supreme Military Council (sometimes renamed Armed Forces Ruling Council) was the apex body under military rule, where major policies and decrees were decided. The Federal Executive Council handled day-to-day administration but was subordinate to it.
questions.p: Di Supreme Military Council (later dem call am Armed Forces Ruling Council) na di highest body under military rule, na dem dey decide big policies and decrees. Federal Executive Council dey handle normal wahala but dem dey under di Supreme Military Council.

questions.q: A major criticism of military rule in Nigeria, from the perspective of federalism, is that it tended to:
o: grant more legislative powers to state houses of assembly
concentrate power at the centre because of the military's hierarchical command structure
increase the number of political parties operating in the states
restore full legislative autonomy to traditional rulers
questions.e: The military operates on a chain of command from the Head of State downward, so this same style was carried into governance, pulling power away from the states to the centre. This weakened true federalism, which requires shared and balanced powers between federal and state levels.
questions.p: Military dey work like chain of command, from Head of State to everybody under am, so dem bring dis same style enter governance, and e pull power comot from states go centre. Dis one weak true federalism wey suppose share power well-well between federal and state.

questions.q: During military rule in Nigeria, decrees issued by the Head of State typically had which of the following effects on existing laws?
o: They required approval by the Senate before they could take effect
They could only amend state laws but never federal laws
They had no binding legal effect until confirmed by the Supreme Court
They could override the constitution and any existing law that was inconsistent with them
questions.e: Military decrees were given supremacy over the constitution and ordinary laws, often including clauses that barred the courts (ouster clauses) from questioning them. This made decrees the main legal tool of military rule.
questions.p: Military decrees dey pass constitution and normal laws, and many times dem dey put clause wey block court from questioning dem (ouster clause). Na so decree come be di main legal tool wey military government dey use rule.

questions.q: According to the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (as amended), how many local government areas are officially recognised in the country?
questions.e: The 1999 Constitution lists exactly 774 local government areas in Nigeria. This number is fixed in the constitution and is a basic fact every candidate should know.
questions.p: Di 1999 Constitution show say Nigeria get 774 local government areas. Dis number dey fixed inside di constitution, na basic fact wey every candidate suppose sabi.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major advantage of the local government system of administration in Nigeria?
o: It brings government and its services closer to the people at the grassroots
It removes the need for state governments to exist
It concentrates all legislative powers in the hands of the federal government
It eliminates the role of traditional rulers in community affairs
questions.e: Local government is the tier of government closest to the people in villages and towns, so it helps deliver services like primary healthcare, markets and sanitation directly to them. The other options describe things local government does not do.
questions.p: Local government na di tier of government wey close pass to di people for village and town, so e dey bring services like health post, market and clean environment reach dem direct. Di other options no be wetin local government dey do.

questions.q: In the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, the specific functions assigned to local government councils are contained in which schedule?
o: Fifth Schedule
Second Schedule
Fourth Schedule
Third Schedule
questions.e: The Fourth Schedule of the 1999 Constitution spells out the functions of local government councils, such as construction of roads, markets and primary education. Candidates must know this because it is often tested directly.
questions.p: Di Fourth Schedule of di 1999 Constitution na im dey list di work wey local government councils suppose do, like road, market and primary school. Dis one dey common for exam so candidates need sabi am well.

questions.q: Local government in Nigeria is commonly described as the 'third tier' of government. This description is based mainly on the fact that it:
o: was the third tier of government to be created historically in Nigeria
has the smallest population compared to the federal and state governments
generates the third largest share of government revenue in the country
occupies the third level in the hierarchical structure of government, below the federal and state governments
questions.e: The term 'third tier' refers to local government's position in the structure of governance, coming after the federal government (first tier) and the state government (second tier). It is about rank in the governmental hierarchy, not about population, history of creation, or revenue size.
questions.p: Dem dey call local government 'third tier' because of how e dey sit for di government structure, after federal (first tier) and state (second tier). E no concern population, history of how dem create am, or how much money e dey generate.

questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria (as amended), the primary responsibility for formulating Nigeria's foreign policy rests with which arm or officer of government?
o: The Nigerian Institute of International Affairs
The Judiciary, through the Supreme Court
The National Assembly, through its Senate Committee on Foreign Affairs
The President, acting through the executive arm of government
questions.e: The Constitution vests executive power, including the conduct of external relations, in the President. The President, assisted by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, formulates and directs Nigeria's foreign policy. The National Assembly only ratifies treaties; it does not formulate policy.
questions.p: Di Constitution give executive power to President, dat one include how Nigeria dey relate wit oda kontri. President, wit di help of Minister of Foreign Affairs, na im dey make di foreign policy. National Assembly na only to confam treaty, dem no dey make di policy.

questions.q: Nigeria's active role in founding the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) in 1963 was mainly an expression of which foreign policy objective?
o: Securing permanent membership of the UN Security Council
Promotion of economic diplomacy with Western powers
Promotion of African unity, solidarity and decolonisation
Protection of Nigerian citizens living abroad
questions.e: The OAU was formed to unite African states, support the liberation of colonies still under foreign rule, and encourage cooperation among African nations. Nigeria, as a leading African power, championed this objective as central to its Afrocentric foreign policy. It was not primarily about trade deals or UN seats.
questions.p: Dem form OAU make African kontris unite, support countries wey still dey under colonial rule, and work together as one. Nigeria, as big African kontri, support dis objective well because im foreign policy dey focus on Africa. E no be about trade deal or UN Security Council seat.

questions.q: During the Cold War era, Nigeria officially pursued a policy of non-alignment. Based on this principle, which of the following actions would have been MOST inconsistent with Nigeria's stated foreign policy?
o: Accepting technical assistance from both the United States and the Soviet Union
Signing a defence pact that ties Nigeria's armed forces exclusively to one superpower bloc
Trading with countries from both the Western and Eastern blocs
Sending delegates to Non-Aligned Movement conferences
questions.e: Non-alignment meant Nigeria refused to be permanently tied to either the Western (capitalist) or Eastern (communist) bloc during the Cold War, so as to relate freely with all nations. Signing an exclusive military pact with one bloc would contradict this neutrality by committing Nigeria firmly to one side. The other options (receiving aid from both sides, trading with both, joining NAM) all fit non-alignment.
questions.p: Non-alignment mean Nigeria no wan tie imsef strong strong to eida di Western (capitalist) or Eastern (communist) side during Cold War, so dat e fit relate well wit everybody. If Nigeria sign military agreement wey go make im army dey only follow one side, dat one go spoil di neutral stand. Di oda options dey match wit non-alignment well well.

questions.q: Which of the following international organisations has its membership restricted only to countries located on the African continent?
o: African Union (AU)
United Nations (UN)
Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC)
Commonwealth of Nations
questions.e: The African Union is made up only of African states, unlike the UN, Commonwealth, and OPEC, which have members from different continents. This makes it a purely continental organisation.
questions.p: African Union na only African kontries dey inside am. UN, Commonwealth, and OPEC get members from different continents, but AU na only Africa.

questions.q: Under the ECOWAS Protocol on Free Movement of Persons, what right is granted to citizens of member states travelling within the sub-region?
o: The right to hold a government ministerial post in another member state
The right to enter and stay in another member state for up to 90 days without a visa
Automatic citizenship of any member state after six months
The right to vote in the national elections of any member state
questions.e: The ECOWAS Protocol allows citizens of member states to enter another member country visa-free and stay for up to 90 days, promoting regional integration. It does not grant automatic citizenship, voting rights, or government positions.
questions.p: ECOWAS Protocol give citizens power to waka enter another member kontri witout visa and stay for 90 days. E no mean say dem go automatically become citizen, vote, or hold government post.

questions.q: A member country of OPEC wants to help raise the global price of crude oil. Based on OPEC's usual method of controlling oil prices, what should this country do?
o: Increase its production above its agreed quota
Withdraw from OPEC and sell oil at any price it wants
Fix oil prices directly with each buyer nation
Comply with an OPEC-agreed cut in its production quota
questions.e: OPEC controls global oil prices mainly by agreeing on production quotas among members; cutting output reduces supply and pushes prices up. Increasing production or acting independently would work against this goal.
questions.p: OPEC dey control oil price by make members agree to cut how much oil dem go produce; if supply reduce, price go rise. If kontri increase production or waka comot to sell anyhow, e no go help raise price.

questions.q: The Commonwealth of Nations mainly promotes cooperation among its member countries in which of these areas?
o: Adoption of a single currency and customs union
Formation of a joint military defence pact
Democracy, human rights, trade and development cooperation
Religious integration policies for all members
questions.e: The Commonwealth focuses on promoting democracy, human rights, trade, and development among its member states, which share historical ties to Britain. It is not a military alliance, a currency union, or a religious body.
questions.p: Commonwealth dey focus on promote democracy, human rights, trade, and development among im members wey get historical connection to Britain. E no be military alliance, currency union, or religious group.

questions.q: Which of the following best illustrates the use of 'coercive power' by a government?
o: The police forcefully disperse and arrest traders occupying an illegal site after warnings were ignored
A town union organises a meeting to discuss community development
A traditional ruler appeals to elders to settle a land dispute
A governor persuades traders to relocate by explaining the benefits of a new market
questions.e: Coercive power involves the use of force or threat of force to compel obedience. Persuasion, appeals, and meetings are not coercive methods.
questions.p: Coercive power mean say government use force or threat to make people obey. Since police use force to move traders, na that one be the correct example.

questions.q: A new government that came to power through a coup later organised a national referendum which most citizens participated in and accepted its rule. This process mainly helped the government to gain:
o: Federalism
Autonomy
Sovereignty
Legitimacy
questions.e: Legitimacy is the popular acceptance of a government's right to rule. The referendum and citizens' acceptance show the government earning legitimacy despite its forceful origin.
questions.p: Legitimacy na when people agree say government get right to rule them. Even if government start with coup, if people accept them through referendum, they don get legitimacy.

questions.q: Popular sovereignty is best described as the principle that:
o: Ultimate political power belongs to the citizens of a state
The courts have final power to interpret all laws
The military retains ultimate control over the state
The head of state cannot be challenged in office
questions.e: Popular sovereignty means supreme power rests with the people, who can exercise it directly or through elected representatives. The other options describe different concepts like judicial or military power.
questions.p: Popular sovereignty mean say the real power dey for hand of the people. Na the citizens get the final say for how their country go run.

questions.q: A community council decides that an issue affecting every household, such as building a new borehole, should be voted on by all adult members of the community rather than by their elected representatives. This practice best reflects:
o: Representative democracy
Theocracy
Monarchy
Direct democracy
questions.e: When citizens themselves vote directly on an issue instead of leaving it to elected representatives, this is direct democracy in action, as practised in small communities or referenda.
questions.p: Direct democracy na when all the people come together to vote on matter by theirsef. Instead of make representative do am, everybody participate directly.

questions.q: Which of the following is a necessary condition for a state to be regarded as sovereign under international law?
o: It must practise a democratic system of government
It must have a large population exceeding 50 million
It must be a member of a regional trade organisation
It must possess independence and freedom from external control in managing its affairs
questions.e: Sovereignty under international law requires that a state is independent and free from external control in conducting its own affairs. Population size, trade membership, and type of government are not requirements for sovereignty.
questions.p: For international law, state must be independent and no external power suppose dey control am. Population or type of government no be the main thing for sovereignty.

questions.q: Charismatic authority, as identified by Max Weber, is best illustrated by a leader whose followers obey because of the leader's:
o: position as the eldest son of the former ruler
control of the national police and army
exceptional personal qualities and ability to inspire loyalty
appointment through a written constitution
questions.e: Charismatic authority rests on the extraordinary personal qualities, vision or appeal of an individual leader that inspire devotion. Inheritance reflects traditional authority, while written rules reflect legal-rational authority.
questions.p: Charismatic authority dey base on person special character and how e fit inspire people. Na wetin make followers dey follow leader because of im personal quality, no be because of law or tradition.

questions.q: Which of the following best distinguishes 'influence' from 'power' in the study of government?
o: Influence relies on persuasion while power may involve the ability to compel obedience
Influence and power are identical concepts with no real difference
Influence is always backed by law while power is never backed by law
Influence can only be exercised by the state while power belongs to individuals
questions.e: Power includes the capacity to compel or force compliance, sometimes through sanctions, while influence works mainly through persuasion and appeal without compulsion. This distinction is important in political analysis.
questions.p: Power fit force person to do wetin you want, but influence na just to persuade person make e agree. Power fit get force inside, but influence na just appeal.

questions.q: A newly elected Local Government Chairman in Kwara State takes the oath of office and immediately begins issuing directives that council workers obey without resistance. This situation best illustrates that his power has been transformed into:
o: federalism
anarchy
authority
sovereignty
questions.e: When power is recognised as rightful and is obeyed willingly because of the office held, it becomes authority. Sovereignty refers to supreme independent power of a state, not an individual official's recognised right to command.
questions.p: When people agree to obey person because dem know say e get right to command, na authority be dat. Sovereignty na supreme power of state, but authority na wetin official get to make people follow am.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly explains the relationship between legitimacy and sovereignty in a modern state?
o: Legitimacy and sovereignty are two names for the same concept
Sovereignty depends entirely on recognition by foreign states while legitimacy does not
A sovereign government automatically enjoys legitimacy among its citizens
Legitimacy strengthens a government's exercise of its sovereign powers by securing willing obedience
questions.e: A government may hold sovereign power yet lack legitimacy if citizens do not accept its right to rule, making enforcement difficult. Legitimacy makes the exercise of sovereign authority smoother because people obey willingly rather than out of fear alone.
questions.p: Legitimacy dey make government work easy because people go obey willingly. Even if government get power, if people no believe say dem get right to rule, e go hard to govern.

questions.q: In political science, 'power' is most accurately described as the:
o: formal recognition given to a government by other states
ability of a person or group to make others act according to their wishes, even against their will
moral right of a ruler to be obeyed by citizens
set of written rules guiding the conduct of government business
questions.e: Power is the capacity to make others comply with one's wishes, whether they agree willingly or not, and may be backed by force. Moral right to be obeyed describes authority, not power itself.
questions.p: Power na the ability to make people do wetin you want, even if dem no like am. E fit involve force, unlike authority wey be say people dey obey because dem respect the office.

questions.q: Which of the following is the clearest example of direct democracy in practice?
o: Citizens of a small Swiss canton gathering to vote directly on a proposed local tax law
Nigerians electing members of the House of Representatives to make laws on their behalf
A political party selecting its presidential candidate through delegates at a convention
A state governor appointing commissioners to run government ministries
questions.e: Direct democracy occurs when citizens themselves make decisions on issues without intermediaries, as seen in small communities or cantons voting directly on laws. Electing representatives, as in Nigeria's National Assembly, is representative democracy instead.
questions.p: Direct democracy mean say the people demsef go vote on top law directly. No be to send representative go house, na the people go decide wetin dem want.

questions.q: A country's constitution states that ultimate lawmaking power rests with the National Assembly, which can amend any law including the constitution following due process, and no other body can override its decisions once properly made. This describes which type of sovereignty?
o: Titular sovereignty
Legal sovereignty
Popular sovereignty
De facto sovereignty
questions.e: Legal sovereignty refers to the body recognised by law as having the supreme, final authority to make and amend laws within a state. Popular sovereignty instead refers to the idea that ultimate power belongs to the people as a whole.
questions.p: Legal sovereignty na the body wey law give the final power to make or change law. No other body fit override wetin dem decide according to the constitution.

questions.q: One major difference between a democratic government and most military regimes is that in a democracy, political power is:
o: acquired through periodic, free and fair elections conducted among the citizens
concentrated permanently in the hands of one unelected individual
seized and maintained mainly through the use of armed force
exercised without any check from the judiciary or legislature
questions.e: Democracy is characterised by leaders gaining power through free and fair elections in which citizens choose their representatives. Military regimes typically take power by force rather than through an electoral process.
questions.p: For democracy, na election be the way wey people take choose who go lead dem. Military regime no dey use election, dem dey take power by force.

questions.q: In Nigeria's federal arrangement, both the Federal Government and the 36 states can make laws on certain matters such as education and agriculture. This list of shared legislative powers is called the
o: Residual legislative list
Exclusive legislative list
Fundamental objectives list
Concurrent legislative list
questions.e: The concurrent legislative list contains matters on which both the federal and state governments can legislate. The exclusive list belongs only to the centre, while residual powers belong only to the states.
questions.p: Concurrent legislative list na di list wey Federal and State government fit make law for inside. Exclusive list na only Federal get am, while residual list na only State get am.

questions.q: Which of the following is the clearest reason why a federal system is often preferred in a country with many ethnic groups, such as Nigeria?
o: It guarantees that all citizens speak one official language
It removes the need for a written constitution
It allows diverse groups to control local affairs while remaining united under one country
It prevents any form of political party competition
questions.e: Federalism allows different ethnic or regional groups to manage their own local affairs through state or regional governments while still being joined together under a central government. This balance helps manage diversity and reduce agitation for secession.
questions.p: Federalism allow different tribes to manage their own local matter while dem still dey one country. E dey help reduce fight and make everybody feel say dem belong.

questions.q: A country has a king as head of state, but the real executive power is exercised by an elected Prime Minister and Cabinet who are responsible to Parliament. This arrangement best describes a
o: Constitutional monarchy
Presidential republic
Absolute monarchy
Theocratic monarchy
questions.e: In a constitutional monarchy, the monarch is a ceremonial head of state while actual governing power lies with elected officials like the Prime Minister. This differs from an absolute monarchy where the king or queen holds full political power.
questions.p: For constitutional monarchy, di king or queen na just ceremonial head, but di real power dey for hand of elected people like Prime Minister. Absolute monarchy different because di king get all di power.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major argument in favour of a unitary system of government over a federal system?
o: It guarantees a hereditary head of state
It gives states the power to create their own constitutions
It allows regions to secede freely
It promotes uniform policies and avoids duplication of government functions
questions.e: A unitary system concentrates power at the centre, which makes it easier to apply the same policies nationwide and avoid the cost of duplicating ministries and agencies at regional levels. Federal systems, by contrast, often involve separate structures for each unit.
questions.p: Unitary system put all power for center, so e dey easy to make one law for everybody. E still dey save money because you no go need duplicate ministries for every state.

questions.q: A republic is best distinguished from a monarchy mainly on the basis of
o: The number of political parties allowed
Whether the country has a written constitution
How the head of state emerges, whether by election or heredity
The size of the country's population
questions.e: The key difference lies in how the head of state comes to power: in a republic, the head of state is elected, while in a monarchy, the position is usually inherited. Other features like constitutions or party systems can exist in both forms of government.
questions.p: Di main difference be say for republic, dem dey elect head of state, but for monarchy, na family line dem dey take inherit am. Other things like constitution fit dey for both.

questions.q: Nigeria operates as a federal republic. Which combination of features correctly justifies this description?
o: Appointed head of state and loose alliance of independent states
Elected head of state and power shared between central and state governments
Hereditary head of state and single-tier government
Elected head of state and all powers concentrated at the centre
questions.e: Nigeria is a republic because its head of state is elected, not hereditary, and it is federal because power is constitutionally divided between the central government and the states. A unitary or confederal description would not fit this dual structure.
questions.p: Nigeria na republic because we dey elect our president, and we be federal because power dey shared between federal and state government. If power dey only for center, e no go be federal again.

questions.q: A key weakness of a monarchy, especially an absolute one, as a form of government is that
o: It allows frequent changes of leadership through elections
It cannot have a constitution of any kind
Succession and policy direction may depend on one family's will rather than the people's choice
It automatically guarantees fair representation of all regions
questions.e: In an absolute monarchy, the throne and major decisions often pass within one ruling family, so citizens have little or no say in choosing their leader or shaping policy direction. This is different from republics where leaders are usually chosen through elections.
questions.p: For absolute monarchy, na one family dey decide everything, so people no get say for who go lead dem. E no be like republic where election dey allow people choose their leader.

questions.q: Two independent states, Alpha and Beta, agree to cooperate only on defence and trade, but each retains full control over its laws, currency, and the right to withdraw from the agreement at any time. This arrangement is best described as
o: A confederation
A federation
A constitutional monarchy
A unitary union
questions.e: A confederation is a loose association of independent states that cooperate on limited matters while keeping their sovereignty and the right to withdraw. This differs from a federation, where the central government has binding authority and states cannot simply leave.
questions.p: Confederation na loose agreement between independent countries to work together for small things like trade. Each country still get their full power and dem fit comot from di agreement anytime.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of the legislature checking the judiciary in a presidential democracy like Nigeria?
o: The Senate overrides a presidential veto on a bill
The judiciary interprets the constitution
The President grants pardon to a convicted offender
The Senate confirms the appointment of judges of the Supreme Court
questions.e: The Senate's power to confirm or reject judicial appointments is a legislative check on the judiciary. The other options involve different arms acting, not the legislature checking the judiciary.
questions.p: Senate get power to approve or reject judge wey dem appoint for Supreme Court. Dis one na how legislature dey check judiciary work so dat power no go too much for one side.

questions.q: A presidential system of government is best described as one in which
o: the legislature and executive are fused into a single body with shared membership
the Head of State and Head of Government are combined in one person who is not a member of the legislature
the Prime Minister is elected by and remains a member of the legislature
the judiciary appoints the Head of Government
questions.e: Under a presidential system, the President serves as both Head of State and Head of Government and is usually not a sitting member of the legislature, unlike in a parliamentary system.
questions.p: For presidential system, one person be Head of State and Head of Government. Dat person no suppose dey inside legislature as member.

questions.q: In a federation practising separation of powers, which situation illustrates the judiciary performing a quasi-legislative function?
o: A court issuing practice directions that regulate how cases are filed in its registry
The President signing an executive order on tax waivers
The National Assembly passing a finance bill into law
A governor dissolving a local government council
questions.e: When courts make rules of procedure that bind litigants, they are effectively creating regulations, which is a law-making (legislative) function performed outside the regular legislature. The other options describe pure executive or legislative acts.
questions.p: When court dey make rules on how dem go dey file case, dem dey do work wey resemble law-making. Dis one na quasi-legislative function because dem dey create regulation for people to follow.

questions.q: One major argument put forward in support of the doctrine of separation of powers is that it
o: speeds up government decision making by concentrating power in one arm
eliminates the need for a written constitution
allows the executive to make, enforce and interpret laws without delay
prevents the concentration of power in a single arm of government, thereby checking tyranny
questions.e: Separation of powers is meant to prevent any one arm from becoming too powerful, thereby protecting citizens from tyranny and abuse of office.
questions.p: Separation of powers dey make sure say power no gather for one hand. E dey help stop tyranny so dat government no go turn to wetin dem like.

questions.q: Which of the following best illustrates fusion of powers rather than separation of powers?
o: A legislator who must resign before accepting a ministerial appointment
A minister who is also an elected member of parliament sitting in the cabinet
A president who cannot be a member of the legislature while in office
A judge who cannot hold any legislative or executive post
questions.e: Fusion of powers occurs where the same person belongs to more than one arm of government, as seen in parliamentary systems where ministers remain sitting members of parliament.
questions.p: Fusion of powers mean say one person dey belong to two arms of government at the same time. Like for parliamentary system, person fit be minister and still dey sit as member of parliament.

questions.q: A notable criticism of the theory of separation of powers, as observed in practice, is that
o: it always leads to a single all-powerful ruler
it prevents the judiciary from ever reviewing executive actions
it is impossible to achieve complete separation since the arms must still cooperate to function effectively
it abolishes the need for elections into public office
questions.e: In practice, no government achieves total separation because the arms must interact and cooperate, for example the executive implements laws passed by the legislature, showing that absolute separation is unrealistic.
questions.p: For real life, e hard to get total separation of powers because the three arms must work together. Dem need each other to run government well, so absolute separation no dey possible.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the principle of separation of powers as applied to the structure of government?
o: The appointment of one person to head the legislature, executive and judiciary at the same time
The vesting of the three governmental functions of law-making, law-execution and law-interpretation in three separate and independent organs
The transfer of all powers of government to the executive arm alone
The sharing of all government revenue equally among the three arms of government
questions.e: Separation of powers means that the three main functions of government are assigned to three distinct and independent organs so that no single arm dominates. It is not about sharing revenue or concentrating power in one arm.
questions.p: Separation of powers mean say make dem share government work into three different independent part so that one person no go carry all power. E no mean say dem dey share money or put all power for one hand.

questions.q: A new state is being created and its drafters want each of the three arms of government to be occupied by different sets of persons, with none of them serving in more than one arm at the same time. This requirement best reflects which rule associated with separation of powers?
o: The rule of delegated legislation
The rule of fusion of functions
The rule against plural membership
The rule of unity of command
questions.e: The rule against plural membership states that a person should not be a member of more than one arm of government at the same time, which strengthens separation of powers. The other options describe different or opposite concepts.
questions.p: The rule against plural membership talk say person no suppose dey work for two different arms of government at the same time. E dey make separation of powers strong well well.

questions.q: Below is a description of a country's government structure: the President, as head of the executive, has the power to appoint judges to the highest courts, subject to confirmation by the Senate. This arrangement is best described as an example of
o: the executive checking the judiciary, moderated by legislative approval
complete separation of powers with no overlap
the judiciary checking the executive directly
fusion of the executive and judiciary into one body
questions.e: Presidential appointment of judges, subject to Senate confirmation, shows the executive exercising a check on the judiciary while the legislature further moderates that power. It is not a case of fusion or judicial control over the executive.
questions.p: When president appoint judge and senate come confirm am, na executive dey check judiciary with senate help. E no mean say dem join body together as one.

questions.q: One of the strongest arguments for separation of powers is that it helps to prevent the abuse of power. This is mainly because the doctrine
o: removes the need for a written constitution
concentrates all state power in the hands of the most experienced arm
eliminates the possibility of conflict among the three arms
allows each arm of government to act as a watchdog over the others
questions.e: By placing law-making, law-execution and law-interpretation in different hands, each arm can monitor and restrain the others, reducing the chances of tyranny. It does not eliminate conflict or concentrate power.
questions.p: E dey prevent abuse of power because each arm dey watch each other like security. E dey make sure say tyranny no happen for country.

questions.q: In a certain federation, the legislature has the exclusive power to approve the annual budget proposed by the executive before any money can be spent from the treasury. This power of the legislature over the executive is best described as
o: power of judicial review
power of impeachment
power of the purse
power of veto override
questions.e: The power of the purse refers to the legislature's control over public funds, including its authority to approve or reject the budget, which checks executive spending. Impeachment and veto override are different legislative checks.
questions.p: Power of the purse na when legislature get control over money and must approve budget before executive spend anything. E be serious check on executive pocket.

questions.q: Suppose the Senate of a country refuses to confirm a presidential nominee for the position of a Minister because the Senate considers the nominee unsuitable. This action is a clear illustration of which function of the legislature within the system of checks and balances?
o: Confirmatory function
Appropriation function
Law-making function
Oversight function over the judiciary
questions.e: When the legislature screens and approves or rejects executive nominees, it is performing its confirmatory function, which checks the appointment powers of the executive. This is distinct from law-making or appropriation.
questions.p: When senate refuse to confirm person wey president choose, na confirmatory function dem dey do. E dey help check executive appointment power.

questions.q: A political analyst argues that although Nigeria practises separation of powers at the federal level, pure separation is practically impossible to achieve in any modern government. Which of the following best supports this argument?
o: The three arms of government never interact with one another under any constitution
Certain functions naturally overlap, such as the executive issuing regulations that have the force of law
The judiciary is completely abolished in most modern constitutions
Each arm of government performs only its own function and nothing else at all times
questions.e: In practice, arms of government often perform functions beyond their primary role, such as the executive making subsidiary legislation, showing that strict separation is difficult to maintain. The judiciary is not abolished, and the arms do interact.
questions.p: For real life, pure separation hard to see because some work dey overlap, like when executive dey make rules wey be like law. E no mean say dem abolish judiciary.

questions.q: Which of these is the best example of a constitution derived mainly from a nation's historical customs, judicial decisions and traditions rather than from a single codified document?
o: The Constitution of the Republic of Ghana
The Constitution of the United States of America
The Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999
The Constitution of the United Kingdom
questions.e: Britain's constitution is built up from customs, traditions, judicial precedents and statutes over centuries, without one single written document. The other three countries have single codified constitutional documents.
questions.p: Na Britain constitution dem dey build from customs, traditions, and court decisions over many years, instead of one single written book. Di other three countries get their own for one single written book.

questions.q: A federal constitution, as a type, is best defined as one in which
o: the legislature can amend any part of the constitution by simple majority vote
the head of state and head of government are combined in one office
all powers are concentrated in a single central authority that creates local governments at will
power is shared between a central government and component states, each supreme in its own sphere
questions.e: A federal constitution divides powers between the central government and the federating units, with each level having exclusive authority in defined areas. The other options describe unitary systems or unrelated features.
questions.p: Federal constitution dey share power between di center government and di state governments, where each level get power for im own area. Di other options dey talk about unitary system or other things wey no consign federation.

questions.q: Nigeria's 1999 Constitution (as amended) is often classified as both written and rigid. Which combination of features best justifies this classification?
o: It is based mainly on unwritten customs but requires a referendum for every amendment
It exists in a single codified document and can only be amended through a special procedure requiring more than a simple majority
It is partly written and partly unwritten, with amendments made informally by convention
It exists in a single codified document but can be changed by ordinary legislation like any other law
questions.e: The 1999 Constitution is contained in one formal document, making it written, and amendments need special majorities in the National and State Assemblies, making it rigid. Ordinary legislative majorities and informal conventions do not apply to its amendment process.
questions.p: Di 1999 Constitution dey inside one book, na why dem call am written constitution, and e dey hard to change because e need special majority for National and State Assemblies. Ordinary law no fit change am easily.

questions.q: Judicial precedents are regarded as a historical source of a constitution mainly because
o: past court decisions interpreting constitutional provisions guide later cases and shape constitutional meaning over time
judges are empowered to rewrite the constitution whenever they consider it outdated
courts alone can create new constitutions without reference to any assembly
the legislature is bound to copy every court ruling into the constitution
questions.e: When courts interpret constitutional provisions, their decisions build a body of precedent that influences how the constitution is understood and applied afterward. Judges interpret rather than rewrite the constitution, and legislatures are not obliged to codify every ruling.
questions.p: When court interpret constitution, di decisions wey dem make dey guide future cases and help people understand di constitution better. Judges dey explain law, dem no dey rewrite am.

questions.q: A student claims that any country with a written constitution automatically has a flexible one. Which statement best corrects this claim?
o: Written constitutions are always rigid, while unwritten ones are always flexible without exception
A constitution's flexibility depends only on the number of pages it contains
Whether a constitution is flexible or rigid depends on its amendment procedure, not on whether it is written or unwritten
Flexibility is determined by how old the constitution is, not by its amendment rules
questions.e: Flexibility or rigidity is decided by how easily a constitution can be amended, which is a separate question from whether it is written down. Some written constitutions are flexible, just as some unwritten ones can be difficult to change in practice.
questions.p: Whether constitution dey flexible or rigid na how dem dey take amend am, and e no mean say because e write down e must hard to change. Some written constitutions dey easy to amend, while some no be so.

questions.q: A confederal arrangement differs from a true federation mainly in that
o: only one level of government exists, with no division of powers at all
member states lose their individual legal identity completely once they join
the central government has supreme authority over all member states in every matter
member states retain greater sovereignty and can withdraw, with the central body having only limited delegated powers
questions.e: In a confederation, independent states cooperate loosely, keep most of their sovereignty, and can leave the union, while the central authority has only limited powers granted to it. This is unlike a federation, where power-sharing is constitutionally entrenched and withdrawal is not simple.
questions.p: For confederal system, member states still hold their power and fit comot anytime, while di center government get small power wey dem give am. E different from federation where power-sharing strong well well inside constitution.

questions.q: Which of the following best illustrates a constitutional convention operating alongside a written constitution?
o: A Supreme Court judgment striking down a law as unconstitutional
The long-standing practice whereby a Nigerian President consults party leaders before certain appointments, though this is not written in the constitution
A constitutional amendment passed by two-thirds majority of the National Assembly
The formal provision in the constitution stating the procedure for electing the President
questions.e: Conventions are unwritten political practices that are followed by custom and expectation, even though they are not legally enforceable or stated in the constitution. The other options describe written provisions, judicial action, or formal amendment, not conventions.
questions.p: Constitutional conventions na unwritten political habits wey people dey follow because of custom, even though dem no write am inside constitution. Di other options na written laws, court judgment, or formal amendments.

questions.q: A textbook author argues that academic writings and legal commentaries on constitutional principles should be seen as a source of constitutional law. This view best reflects which category of source?
o: A historical source that automatically becomes law once published
A formal source equal in authority to an act of the legislature
Persuasive but non-binding secondary source that influences interpretation
Primary material source with the same binding force as the written text
questions.e: Scholarly writings can influence how courts and lawmakers understand constitutional provisions, but they are not legally binding by themselves. They only persuade interpretation; they do not carry the same force as the constitution's actual text or enacted laws.
questions.p: Book writings and legal opinions fit help court and law makers understand constitution well, but dem no be binding law on their own. Na just to guide interpretation dem dey use am, dem no get power like main text.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of Dicey's three main principles of the Rule of Law?
o: Concentration of power in a single arm of government
Equality of all persons before the law
Supremacy of ordinary law over arbitrary power
The constitution is a result of the ordinary law of the land
questions.e: Dicey's rule of law rests on supremacy of law, equality before the law, and the constitution being derived from ordinary law. Concentrating power in one arm of government contradicts the rule of law and separation of powers.
questions.p: Dicey talk say law get supremacy, equality, and say constitution come from ordinary law. To put all power for one hand no be Rule of Law at all.

questions.q: A derogation (limitation) clause in the Nigerian Constitution allows the government to restrict certain fundamental rights mainly in order to:
o: Give the executive control over the judiciary
Protect public safety, public order, morality or the rights of others
Reduce the number of political parties
Increase the powers of traditional rulers
questions.e: Derogation clauses permit reasonable limitation of some rights when necessary to protect public order, safety, health, morality or the rights of other citizens. This is a recognised constitutional safeguard, not a tool for political control.
questions.p: Derogation clause mean say government fit limit some rights if e go help protect public safety or morality. E no be say dem wan use am control people anyhow.

questions.q: Which of these is best described as a third-generation (solidarity) right rather than a civil or socio-economic right?
o: Right to freedom of movement
Right to a fair hearing
Right to clean and healthy environment
Right to own property
questions.e: Third-generation rights are collective 'solidarity' rights such as the right to a clean environment and development, which benefit whole communities. Fair hearing, movement and property are civil/political or first-generation rights.
questions.p: Third-generation rights na rights wey concern everybody for community, like clean environment. Dem no be like civil rights wey be individual matter.

questions.q: In a town in Kano State, soldiers demolished a trader's shop without a court order simply because he was suspected of hoarding goods. This action is best described as a violation of:
o: The concept of ministerial responsibility
The doctrine of separation of powers only
The principle of federal character
The rule of law through self-help by state agents
questions.e: Demolishing property without due process and a court order is an arbitrary act of self-help that breaches the rule of law, which requires that no one be punished except through established legal procedure. It does not primarily concern federal character or ministerial responsibility.
questions.p: If soldier break person shop without court order, na self-help be dat. Rule of Law talk say dem must follow due process before dem punish anybody.

questions.q: A key difference between fundamental human rights and other legal rights in Nigeria is that fundamental rights:
o: Are specifically entrenched in the Constitution and enforceable in court
Are granted only during a state of emergency
Depend entirely on an Act of the National Assembly for their existence
Can only be enjoyed by government officials
questions.e: Fundamental human rights are written into the Constitution and can be directly enforced in court, unlike ordinary legal rights created by statute. They exist independent of any special emergency situation.
questions.p: Fundamental human rights dey inside Constitution and you fit go court if dem violate am. E no be like ordinary law wey National Assembly fit just change anyhow.

questions.q: A state government enacts a law stating that only citizens from a particular ethnic group may be employed in its civil service. A court is most likely to strike down this law because it violates the constitutional provision on:
o: Right to freedom of association
Right to fair hearing
Right to freedom from discrimination
Freedom of information
questions.e: Restricting employment to one ethnic group directly contravenes the constitutional right to freedom from discrimination, which guarantees equal treatment regardless of ethnic origin. It is not primarily about fair hearing, association, or information.
questions.p: If state government talk say na only one tribe fit work for civil service, dat one na discrimination. Constitution no gree make dem treat people anyhow because of where dem come from.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major function performed by political parties but NOT by pressure groups in a democracy?
o: Making representations to the press
Organizing public enlightenment campaigns
Lobbying government officials on specific issues
Sponsoring candidates for elective offices
questions.e: Political parties exist mainly to win elections by sponsoring candidates for office. Pressure groups do not sponsor candidates; they only try to influence those already in power.
questions.p: Political party get main aim to win election by putting candidates for office. Pressure group no dey sponsor candidate; dem only dey try change wetin government dey do.

questions.q: A country's constitution allows citizens to form as many political parties as they wish, and elections usually produce several parties represented in parliament, none of which can govern alone. This describes a system of government based on a:
o: two-party system
multi-party system
one-party system
dominant-party system
questions.e: A multi-party system allows numerous parties to contest elections freely, often leading to coalition governments since no single party wins outright. This differs from systems with only one or two major parties.
questions.p: Multi-party system allow plenty parties to contest election freely. Because no single party fit win everything, dem dey often join hand form coalition government.

questions.q: One major criticism of the two-party system, as practised in countries like the United States, is that it:
o: limits the range of political choices available to voters
makes it difficult for any government to be formed after elections
promotes constant collapse of government due to defections
encourages excessive formation of weak coalition governments
questions.e: With only two major parties dominating politics, voters with views outside these two platforms have fewer alternatives to choose from. Coalition problems and government collapse are more associated with multi-party systems.
questions.p: When only two parties dey control politics, voters no get plenty choice. People wey get different ideas no get many option to pick from.

questions.q: During Nigeria's Fourth Republic, market women under the Nigeria Association of Petty Traders and Petty Traders refused to pay a newly introduced levy and organized peaceful protests until the local government suspended the levy. This action best illustrates a pressure group using which method?
o: Formation of a splinter political party
Direct mass action to compel a policy reversal
Filing a suit at the Federal High Court
Sponsorship of candidates for local government elections
questions.e: The traders used protest and refusal to comply as a form of direct mass action to pressure the government into reversing its decision. This is a common pressure group tactic that does not involve contesting elections or going to court.
questions.p: Those traders use protest and refusal to pay tax as direct action to force government change mind. Na common way wey pressure group dey use get wetin dem want.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why military regimes in Nigeria's history typically banned political parties but could not completely eliminate pressure group activities?
o: Pressure groups do not seek to capture political power, so they posed less direct threat
Pressure groups operate only outside the country
Pressure groups are smaller in membership than political parties
Pressure groups are usually registered with the military government unlike parties
questions.e: Military governments banned parties because parties aim to capture state power through elections, which threatens military rule. Pressure groups merely seek to influence policy without contesting for power, making them harder to fully suppress and less politically threatening.
questions.p: Military government dey fear political party because party want take power through election. Pressure group no want power, so military no dey see dem as big threat.

questions.q: A key difference between the one-party system practised in some African states after independence and a dominant-party system found in some modern democracies is that in a dominant-party system:
o: the government is usually formed by the military
there are no elections conducted at all
opposition parties are legally permitted but rarely win power
only one party is legally allowed to exist
questions.e: In a dominant-party system, other parties can legally form and contest elections, but one party consistently wins due to its popularity or structural advantages. A one-party system, by contrast, legally bans all other parties from existing.
questions.p: For dominant-party system, other parties fit exist and contest election, but one party just dey win always. One-party system no allow any other party to exist at all.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most important factor that determines whether a country develops a two-party system rather than a multi-party system?
o: The number of ethnic groups in the country
The level of literacy among the electorate
The size of the country's population
The electoral system in use, especially a simple plurality (first-past-the-post) method
questions.e: A simple plurality electoral system tends to squeeze out small parties because only the candidate with the highest votes wins, encouraging voters and politicians to concentrate around two major parties. Proportional representation, by contrast, favours multi-party systems.
questions.p: Dis kind system dey make am hard for small parties to win because na only person wey get highest votes dey win. E dey make voters and politicians join hand support only two major parties.

questions.q: During the First Republic in Nigeria, political parties such as the NPC, NCNC and AG were formed mainly along what basis?
o: Trade union affiliations
Regional and ethnic groupings
Religious doctrines
Military backing
questions.e: The major parties of the First Republic drew their strongest support from particular regions and ethnic groups, such as the North, East and West. This regional character later contributed to political instability.
questions.p: The main parties for First Republic get strong support from dia own region and tribe like North, East and West. Dis regional way wey dem follow run matter later cause plenty wahala for politics.

questions.q: A political party that wins an election forms the government, while the party or parties that lose form the official opposition. What is the main constitutional role of the opposition party in a democracy?
o: To dissolve the ruling party through court action
To replace the ruling party immediately after losing an election
To automatically take over government appointments
To check and criticise government actions and policies in order to keep it accountable
questions.e: The opposition's role is to scrutinise, criticise and offer alternative policies to the ruling party, thereby promoting accountability and good governance. It does not have power to dissolve or immediately replace the government outside elections.
questions.p: Work of opposition na to shine eye, criticize government, and show another better way wey dem fit do things. Dem no get power to just scatter government or change am anyhow outside election.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a 'manifesto' as used by political parties during election campaigns?
o: A list of court judgements against the party
A certificate issued by the electoral body to winning candidates
A document stating the party's aims, policies and programmes if voted into power
A register containing the names of registered voters
questions.e: A manifesto is the official statement of a party's intended policies and programmes, used to persuade voters during campaigns. It is different from a voters' register or a certificate of return.
questions.p: Manifesto na the book wey party write to show wetin dem wan do for people if dem win election. E different from register for voters or paper wey dem dey give winner.

questions.q: In which of the following ways do pressure groups most commonly influence government policy without contesting elections?
o: By lobbying, lobbying officials, organising public awareness campaigns and making representations to government
By forming an alternative government after elections
By presenting a list of candidates for the presidency
By dissolving the National Assembly
questions.e: Pressure groups seek to influence government decisions through lobbying, advocacy, public enlightenment and petitions rather than seeking political power directly through elections. They do not form governments or dissolve legislatures.
questions.p: Pressure groups dey use lobbying, campaign and talking to government make things change instead of to contest election. Dem no dey form government or pack assembly people go house.

questions.q: In a country practising a dominant one-party system where opposition parties legally exist but rarely win any seats over several decades, which of the following best explains this political outcome?
o: The ruling party enjoys overwhelming structural, financial and historical advantages that make genuine competition difficult
Only government workers are allowed to vote
The constitution bans all opposition parties from contesting
Elections are not conducted in that country
questions.e: A dominant-party system allows multiple parties to exist and contest, but one party consistently wins due to advantages such as superior funding, incumbency, patronage networks and historical loyalty. This differs from a one-party state where other parties are legally banned.
questions.p: For dominant-party system, plenty parties dey exist, but na one party dey always win because dem get money, power and history for back. E no mean say law ban other parties.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why professional associations such as the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) are classified as pressure groups rather than political parties?
o: They receive funding directly from the government
They are registered by the Independent National Electoral Commission to contest elections
They seek to influence government decisions on issues affecting their profession without sponsoring candidates for elective office
They have no interest whatsoever in government policies
