questions.e: Pressure groups like the Nigerian Bar Association aim to protect and promote the interests of their members by influencing government policy, but they do not sponsor candidates for elections. This distinguishes them clearly from political parties, which seek political power directly.
questions.p: Pressure groups like NBA dey fight for their members matter and dey advice government, but dem no dey put person for election. Na that one make dem different from political parties.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines an electoral college as a method of election?
o: A system in which traditional rulers nominate candidates for election
A system in which a selected group of representatives votes on behalf of the wider electorate to choose a leader
A system in which ordinary citizens vote directly to choose their leaders
A system in which only party leaders decide who becomes president
questions.e: An electoral college is a body of chosen representatives who formally cast votes to elect a leader instead of the whole electorate voting directly. This differs from direct popular voting, party selection, or nomination by traditional rulers.
questions.p: Electoral college na when selected group of people dey vote on behalf of everybody to choose leader. E different from direct voting or when party leaders just pick person.

questions.q: One key difference between a referendum and a general election is that a referendum is used mainly to
o: choose representatives to occupy legislative seats
appoint judges to the electoral tribunal
select candidates for a political party's primary election
allow citizens to vote directly on a specific issue or proposed law
questions.e: A referendum is a direct vote by citizens on a particular issue, such as approving or rejecting a proposed law or constitutional change, unlike a general election which chooses representatives. Party primaries and judicial appointments are unrelated processes.
questions.p: Referendum na direct vote wey citizens dey use decide on specific issue or law, instead of choosing representatives like for normal election. E no concern party primaries or court matter.

questions.q: A major criticism often raised against the Majority (Second Ballot) electoral system, compared with First-Past-The-Post, is that it
o: guarantees that a candidate wins with less than half of the total votes cast
makes it impossible for more than two candidates to contest an election
can be more expensive and time-consuming because a run-off election may be needed
requires only one round of voting regardless of the number of candidates
questions.e: Under the Majority system, if no candidate secures more than half of the votes in the first round, a second round (run-off) is held, which increases cost and time. This differs from First-Past-The-Post, which needs only one round regardless of the margin of victory.
questions.p: Majority system fit expensive and take time because if nobody get more than half of the votes for first round, dem must do second round run-off. This one different from First-Past-The-Post wey dey need only one round.

questions.q: Which of these is a statutory function of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) besides conducting elections?
o: Monitoring the organisation and operation of political parties, including their finances
Approving the national budget before it is presented to the National Assembly
Prosecuting all criminal cases arising from armed robbery during elections
Appointing state governors in the event of a vacancy
questions.e: INEC is constitutionally empowered to monitor political parties, including their conventions, congresses and finances, in addition to conducting elections. It has no role in appointing governors, approving national budgets, or prosecuting general criminal cases unrelated to its mandate.
questions.p: INEC work no be just to conduct election, dem suppose also monitor how political parties dey run their matter and check their money. Dem no get hand to appoint governor or approve budget.

questions.q: In an election held in a certain constituency, Party A scored 45% of total valid votes, Party B scored 40%, and Party C scored the remaining votes. Under a simple plurality (First-Past-The-Post) system, which statement is correct?
o: Party C automatically wins because it has the smallest share of spoilt votes
The election must be cancelled because no party reached an absolute majority
A run-off must be held between Party A and Party B
Party A wins because it has the highest percentage, even though it did not reach 50%
questions.e: Under First-Past-The-Post, the candidate or party with the highest number of votes wins, even without reaching 50%, since there is no requirement for an absolute majority. This rules out cancellation, a run-off, or any automatic win for the party with fewer votes.
questions.p: For First-Past-The-Post system, anyone wey get the highest vote win, even if e no reach fifty percent. Dem no need any run-off or make dem cancel the election.

questions.q: In the conduct of elections in Nigeria, accreditation of voters before voting is mainly meant to
o: determine the winner of the election immediately
prevent multiple voting and confirm genuine voters
increase the number of registered political parties
reduce the number of polling units in a state
questions.e: Accreditation checks that a person is a genuine, registered voter before being allowed to vote, thereby preventing one person from voting more than once. It has nothing to do with party registration or polling unit numbers.
questions.p: Accreditation dey help make dem confirm say you be real voter before you vote, so nobody go fit vote pass one time. E no get anything to do with party registration.

questions.q: A system of election in which the whole country is treated as a single constituency and parties win seats according to the share of total national votes they obtain is known as
o: constituency delimitation
indirect election
electoral college system
proportional representation
questions.e: Proportional representation allocates seats to parties in line with the percentage of votes won nationally, unlike systems based on winning individual constituencies. Delimitation and electoral college relate to different processes.
questions.p: Proportional representation mean say party go get seats based on the percentage of total national votes wey dem win. E different from system wey person dey win for just one constituency.

questions.q: During the 2023 collation of results for a state House of Assembly seat in Nigeria, a candidate who lost at a polling unit wishes to formally challenge the figures recorded. The most appropriate immediate step is to
o: wait until after inauguration to protest
mobilise supporters to disrupt collation
lodge a complaint with the presiding or collation officer before the result is signed
report directly to the Inspector General of Police
questions.e: Objections to figures should be raised with the presiding or collation officer at the point of collation, before the result sheet is signed, as provided under INEC's result management procedure. Disruption or delayed protest does not follow due process.
questions.p: If you wan complain about election result, you suppose talk to the presiding officer before dem sign am. E no make sense to carry thugs go scatter place or wait till dem swear person in.

questions.q: One major reason why INEC conducts continuous voter registration (CVR) rather than a one-off registration exercise is to
o: allow newly eligible citizens and those who missed earlier exercises to register
ensure only members of the ruling party are registered
reduce the overall cost of printing permanent voter cards
limit the number of people who can vote in an election
questions.e: Continuous voter registration gives citizens who turn eighteen or who were previously unregistered a fair chance to be captured on the voter roll. It is not designed to restrict voting or favour any party.
questions.p: Continuous voter registration dey help people wey just clock eighteen years or wey miss the old time make dem fit register. E dey give everybody open door to register anytime.

questions.q: In a council election, Candidate Uche polled 3,200 votes, Candidate Bello polled 2,850 votes, and Candidate Okafor polled 1,950 votes out of 8,000 valid votes cast. Applying the simple plurality rule, who is declared the winner and why?
o: Okafor, because he had the fewest votes
Uche, because he scored more votes than any other single candidate
No winner, because none scored up to 50% of total votes
Bello, because his votes plus Okafor's exceed Uche's
questions.e: Under simple plurality (First-Past-The-Post), the candidate with the highest individual vote total wins even without reaching half of all votes cast. Uche's 3,200 votes is higher than Bello's or Okafor's, so he wins.
questions.p: Under simple plurality system, the person wey get the highest number of votes win, even if e no reach half of all the votes. Uche get 3,200 votes wey pass everybody, na him win.

questions.q: A key distinguishing feature of a direct election compared to an indirect election is that in a direct election
o: representatives are chosen by members of an electoral college
voters choose their representatives themselves without an intermediary body
the legislature appoints the final office holders
only traditional rulers nominate the candidates
questions.e: A direct election allows ordinary voters to cast ballots directly for the candidates of their choice. Indirect election instead passes the choice through an intermediary such as an electoral college or legislature.
questions.p: Direct election mean say na ordinary voters go straight to vote for the people wey dem want. Dem no dey use electoral college or anybody as middleman.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a 'good citizen' as distinct from a mere legal citizen of a state?
o: A person who was born within the territory of the state
A person who merely holds a national passport issued by government
A person who obeys laws, pays taxes and participates actively in nation building
A person who resides permanently within the boundaries of the state
questions.e: Legal citizenship is a status, but a good citizen goes further by actively performing civic duties such as obeying laws, paying taxes and contributing to development. Mere residence or birth does not guarantee good citizenship.
questions.p: Legal citizen na just paper status, but better citizen dey do pass that one by obeying law and paying tax. Person wey just born for country or dey live there no automatically mean say na better citizen.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major function of public opinion in a democratic society like Nigeria?
o: It replaces the need for elections and political parties
It guarantees that government decisions are never challenged
It ensures that only the wealthy class can influence government decisions
It serves as a check on government excesses by expressing collective approval or disapproval of policies
questions.e: Public opinion acts as a feedback mechanism, allowing citizens to express approval or disapproval of government actions, thereby checking excesses. It does not eliminate elections or restrict influence to the wealthy alone.
questions.p: Public opinion dey help people talk whether dem like government policy abi dem no like am, and dis one dey check government power. E no mean say election no go dey again or say na only rich people fit talk.

questions.q: A town hall survey in Benue State found that 65% of youths interviewed could not name their state governor or local government chairman. This situation is best described as evidence of:
o: Low political awareness arising from poor political socialisation
Effective propaganda by the ruling political party
Strong political socialisation among the youths
High political efficacy in the community
questions.e: Failure to identify basic political office holders shows a gap in political knowledge, which reflects weak political socialisation. This is different from political efficacy, which concerns belief in one's ability to influence government.
questions.p: If youth no know their leaders, e show say political education no reach them well. Dat one na sign of low political awareness, no be say dem get power to influence government.

questions.q: Which of the following best illustrates the role of religious institutions as agents of political socialisation in Nigeria?
o: A religious leader teaching congregants about obedience to just laws and civic responsibility
A church choir performing during a national cultural festival
A religious body building a private hospital for its members
A mosque or church organising a wedding ceremony for its members
questions.e: Religious institutions socialise members politically when they teach values like obedience to just laws, honesty and civic duty, shaping political attitudes. Activities like weddings or building hospitals are social, not political socialisation functions.
questions.p: Church and mosque dey train people politically when dem teach them to obey good laws and do civic duty. Marriage and hospital na normal social work, no be political training.

questions.q: A researcher wants to find out the political opinion of secondary school students across Nigeria on compulsory civic education but only interviews students in one private school in Abuja. Which weakness in opinion measurement does this best illustrate?
o: Excessive use of government-controlled questionnaires
Use of an unrepresentative sample that cannot be generalised to the whole population
Over-reliance on referendum as a method of sampling opinion
Absence of political socialisation among the respondents
questions.e: Studying only one school cannot represent the views of all Nigerian secondary school students because the sample is too narrow and not diverse enough. A valid survey needs a representative sample drawn from different locations and backgrounds.
questions.p: To go interview only one school for Abuja no represent all students for Nigeria because the people wey you ask too small. Proper research suppose carry people from different places join.

questions.q: Which of the following rights is specifically associated with citizenship rather than mere residency in a country?
o: The right to attend any public event open to visitors
The right to travel within the country as a tourist
The right to vote and be voted for in public elections
The right to purchase goods in the local market
questions.e: Voting and contesting elections are political rights reserved for citizens, unlike shopping or sightseeing which any resident or visitor can do. This distinguishes the privileges of citizenship from ordinary residency.
questions.p: Na only citizens get right to vote and contest for election, unlike ordinary residents wey fit just come buy things or travel about. Dis one na the main difference between citizen and resident.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key difference between a citizen and an alien in Nigeria?
o: A citizen can reside in the country while an alien cannot
A citizen pays taxes while an alien does not
A citizen can own property while an alien cannot
A citizen can vote and be voted for while an alien cannot
questions.e: Only citizens enjoy full political rights such as voting and contesting elections. Aliens may own property, reside and pay taxes but are excluded from political participation rights reserved for citizens.
questions.p: Na only citizen get right to vote or contest for election. Even if alien get property or pay tax, dem no get power to participate for politics.

questions.q: A new graduate who has just obtained her voter's card immediately joins a political party, attends ward meetings and volunteers during elections. This behaviour best illustrates which stage or outcome of political socialisation?
o: Political neutrality
Political alienation
Political participation
Political apathy
questions.e: Political participation refers to active involvement in political activities such as joining parties and voting. Her actions show she has been positively socialised into taking an active role in politics, unlike apathy or alienation which involve withdrawal.
questions.p: When person join party and follow do election work, na political participation be dat. E show say the person get interest for how country dey run, e no be apathy.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major advantage of public corporations over civil service departments in the management of commercial ventures?
o: They are fully funded through annual budgetary allocation
They enjoy greater freedom from bureaucratic bottlenecks in decision making
They are headed by permanent secretaries who control daily operations
Their staff are appointed directly by the Federal Civil Service Commission
questions.e: Public corporations are set up as semi-autonomous bodies with their own boards so that they can take quick business decisions without the slow bureaucratic procedures found in civil service departments. The other options describe features of civil service ministries, not public corporations.
questions.p: Dem create public corporations as semi-autonomous bodies so dem fit take quick business decisions without all those slow civil service delays. Na ministries get the other features, not public corporations.

questions.q: In the classical structure of the Nigerian civil service, the hierarchy from the lowest to the highest rank of officers is best arranged as:
o: Permanent Secretary, Director, Assistant Director, Clerical Officer
Assistant Director, Clerical Officer, Director, Permanent Secretary
Director, Permanent Secretary, Executive Officer, Clerical Officer
Clerical Officer, Executive Officer, Assistant Director, Director, Permanent Secretary
questions.e: The civil service is organised as a ladder of ranks, starting from junior clerical staff and rising through executive officers, assistant directors, directors, up to the permanent secretary who is the administrative head of a ministry. Only this order follows the correct bottom-to-top arrangement.
questions.p: Civil service dey arrange like ladder, e dey start from junior clerical staff go up reach executive officers, assistant directors, directors, and permanent secretary. Na only this option show correct arrangement from bottom to top.

questions.q: A board member of a public corporation insists that every contract above a certain amount must first be approved by the supervising government ministry before it can be awarded. This requirement illustrates that public corporations:
o: Are subject to a measure of government supervision despite their separate legal status
Operate completely independently of government control
Cannot enter into contracts without the National Assembly's consent
Function exactly like private limited liability companies
questions.e: Although a public corporation is a separate legal entity with its own board, it still remains accountable to the government that created it, often through ministerial approval for major financial decisions. This shows that corporation autonomy is not absolute but is checked by government oversight.
questions.p: Even though public corporation get im own board, dem still dey accountable to government through ministerial approval for major money matters. This one show say corporation freedom no be absolute, government still dey supervise dem.

questions.q: One major reason why successive Nigerian governments have embarked on the commercialisation of some public corporations, rather than outright privatisation, is to:
o: Convert the corporation into a government ministry
Make the corporation operate on strict profit-making lines while government retains ownership
Remove the corporation entirely from public accountability
Transfer full ownership of the corporation to private shareholders
questions.e: Commercialisation means running a public corporation like a private business, charging economic rates and aiming to make profit, while government still remains the owner. This is different from privatisation, which involves selling government shares to private investors.
questions.p: Commercialisation mean say government wan make the corporation run like private business to make profit, but government still remain the owner. E different from privatisation where dem go sell government shares to private people.

questions.q: The body generally empowered to recruit, promote, transfer and discipline career officers in the federal civil service of Nigeria, excluding politically appointed officials, is the:
o: Federal Civil Service Commission
Independent National Electoral Commission
National Judicial Council
Federal Executive Council
questions.e: The Federal Civil Service Commission handles staff matters such as recruitment, promotion, transfer and discipline of career civil servants at the federal level. The other bodies listed deal with elections, overall policy direction, or the judiciary and not routine civil service staff matters.
questions.p: Na Federal Civil Service Commission dey handle matter like recruitment, promotion, and discipline for federal civil servants. The other bodies na for election, policy, or judiciary, not routine civil service staff work.

questions.q: A new graduate joins the civil service and is told that, regardless of which political party forms the government, she is expected to serve the government of the day loyally and impartially. This expectation best reflects the civil service principle of:
o: Anonymity
Permanency
Hierarchy
Neutrality
questions.e: Neutrality requires civil servants to serve whichever government is in power faithfully, without showing favour to any political party. Permanency refers to continuity of service across changing governments, while anonymity and hierarchy describe other separate features.
questions.p: Neutrality mean say civil servant must serve any government wey enter power faithfully without support any political party. Permanency na for continuity across different governments, while anonymity and hierarchy mean different things.

questions.q: A key difference between a public corporation and a government ministry is that a public corporation:
o: Relies solely on the consolidated revenue fund for its entire running cost
Is headed by a permanent secretary who reports to a minister
Is created directly by an Act of parliament or similar instrument and has a separate legal personality
Forms part of the direct administrative structure of a government ministry
questions.e: A public corporation is usually established by a specific law or decree that gives it a separate legal identity, its own governing board, and the power to sue and be sued in its own name. A ministry, by contrast, is headed by a permanent secretary and is directly part of government administration without separate legal personality.
questions.p: Public corporation get im own separate legal identity and governing board through an Act of parliament, so e fit sue and be sued. Ministry na direct part of government administration wey permanent secretary dey head.

questions.q: Before the Jihad of 1804, the Hausa states such as Kano, Katsina and Zazzau were organized as separate kingdoms, each ruled by a king known as the
o: Sultan
Waziri
Sarki
Emir
questions.e: Before the Fulani Jihad, the Hausa kings bore the title Sarki. The title Emir became common only after the Jihad under the Sokoto Caliphate system.
questions.p: Before di Jihad start, dem dey call Hausa kings Sarki. Na after di Jihad dem come start to dey use Emir for di Sokoto Caliphate system.

questions.q: A major reason the Fulani Jihadists gave for waging war against the Hausa kings in the early 19th century was that the Hausa rulers had
o: mixed Islamic practice with pagan customs and taxed people unjustly
prevented cattle rearers from grazing their herds
refused to pay tribute to Sokoto
allied with European traders against Fulani interests
questions.e: Usman dan Fodio justified the Jihad on religious grounds, accusing Hausa rulers of corrupting Islam with pagan practices and oppressing the people through unjust taxation. This was the central religious and moral justification for the war.
questions.p: Usman dan Fodio talk say di Hausa kings dey mix Islam wit pagan way. E also talk say dem dey tax pipo anyhow, so na dat one make am start di war.

questions.q: In pre-colonial Yoruba kingdoms, the Iyalode was a prominent title given to a woman who
o: served as the chief judge in criminal matters
led the royal bodyguard of the Oba
controlled the palace treasury alone
represented the interests of women in the council of chiefs
questions.e: The Iyalode held a recognized chieftaincy title representing women's affairs and interests, especially traders, in the traditional council. This gave women a formal voice in governance despite being a largely male-dominated system.
questions.p: Iyalode na big title for woman wey dey represent women mata for di council of chiefs. Even though na men dey rule, dis title give women voice for governance.

questions.q: A key difference between the political system of the Yoruba and that of the Igbo in pre-colonial times was that
o: the Yoruba had no form of government while the Igbo had centralized kingdoms
the Yoruba generally operated centralized kingship while the Igbo were mainly organized around village democracy
the Igbo had powerful emirs while the Yoruba had no chiefs
both groups were ruled by a single central monarch
questions.e: Yoruba kingdoms were built around an Oba supported by chiefs, a centralized monarchy. Igbo society, by contrast, was largely republican and acephalous, with authority resting in village assemblies and elders rather than a king.
questions.p: Yoruba pipo get centralized kingship wit Oba, but Igbo pipo no get one central king. Igbo pipo system na village democracy wey elders dey control.

questions.q: In traditional Igbo society, a man who successfully took the highest traditional title through wealth, integrity and community service earned the respected status of
o: Ozo
Diokpa
Ekwueme
Ndichie
questions.e: The Ozo title was a prestigious title taken by wealthy and respected men, giving them social recognition and a voice in community affairs. It was earned, not inherited, reflecting the achievement-based nature of Igbo society.
questions.p: Ozo title na very big achievement for Igbo land. Pipo wey get money and good character dey take am to show say dem get respect for community.

questions.q: The pre-colonial Igbo age-grade system (Otu Ogbo) primarily functioned to
o: select the next Obi through hereditary succession
collect taxes for the Eze on behalf of the colonial government
serve as the personal bodyguards of a central king
organize men of similar age for communal labour, defence and maintenance of order
questions.e: Age grades grouped people born within the same years to perform communal duties such as road clearing, defence and keeping law and order. This system worked alongside the council of elders in the absence of central kingship, reinforcing Igbo republicanism.
questions.p: Age grade system dey group pipo wey get same age to do communal work. Dem dey help clear road, defend di village, and make sure say peace dey.

questions.q: A candidate compares three pre-colonial Nigerian systems: one with a divine king checked by a council that could demand his suicide, one with emirs ruling under a religious caliph, and one with no central ruler but village assemblies of elders. These examples best illustrate differences in
o: the method of tax collection across the three systems
the sources and limits of political authority across the three systems
the economic activities practised by each group
the religious beliefs held before colonial rule
questions.e: The scenario contrasts how power was gained and controlled: divine kingship checked by chiefs, religious authority under a caliph, and decentralized elder-based rule. This directly compares the sources and limitations of political authority in each system.
questions.p: Dis example show how power dey work for different places. E explain how dem dey control authority and who get power to check di leaders.

questions.q: In the pre-colonial Hausa-Fulani political system, the Madawaki held which of the following positions in the emir's administration?
o: Chief Islamic judge
Head of the native treasury
Commander of the cavalry forces
Head of the royal household slaves
questions.e: The Madawaki was the title given to the commander of the cavalry, responsible for organizing and leading the emirate's mounted warriors in battle. He was one of the key military title holders under the emir.
questions.p: Na Madawaki dem dey give dis title as di commander of horse-riders for war. Na him dey organize di warriors to fight for di emirate.

questions.q: A major feature that distinguished the pre-colonial Hausa-Fulani system of government from that of the Yoruba was that the Hausa-Fulani system was based mainly on
o: feudal and theocratic principles rooted in Islamic law
rotation of kingship among ruling age-grades
collective ownership of land by village assemblies alone
a loose confederation of equal villages without central authority
questions.e: After the Jihad, the Hausa-Fulani states were organized as emirates ruled according to Islamic law, with the emir holding both political and religious authority. This feudal-theocratic structure differed from the more secular, council-based Yoruba monarchy.
questions.p: After di Jihad, Hausa-Fulani states come turn to emirates wey dey follow Islamic law. Di emir get both political and religious power, unlike Yoruba system.

questions.q: In pre-colonial Yoruba towns, a settler or stranger who wished to settle permanently was usually required to seek the protection and sponsorship of
o: the Ogboni cult directly
the Aremo of the town
the Oyo Mesi council
a Baale or family head willing to stand as his guarantor
questions.e: Strangers in Yoruba towns were attached to a compound head or Baale who vouched for their conduct and integrated them into the community. This system ensured accountability and social order in the town.
questions.p: If stranger wan settle for Yoruba town, e must find compound head or Baale to stand as guarantor. Dis one dey help to make sure everywhere peaceful.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the position of the Oba in a typical pre-colonial Yoruba kingdom?
o: He ruled as an absolute monarch answerable to no one
He was a sacred ruler whose powers were checked by chiefs and traditional councils
He was elected annually by all adult male members of the town
He was merely a ceremonial figure with no political role
questions.e: The Oba was regarded as sacred and enjoyed great respect, but his actions were checked by councils such as the chiefs and kingmakers. This balance prevented absolute, unchecked rule.
questions.p: Even though dem respect di Oba as sacred king, council of chiefs and kingmakers dey check him powers. E no make am become dictator.

questions.q: In pre-colonial Igbo society, the Umunna system mainly served to
o: train young men exclusively for warfare against neighbouring clans
collect tribute on behalf of a central Igbo king
unite male descendants of a common ancestor for mutual political and social support
regulate trade between Igbo and Hausa merchants
questions.e: The Umunna was a group of men tracing descent from a common ancestor, and it served as a unit of political, social and economic cooperation. It played a key role in settling disputes and maintaining order among its members.
questions.p: Umunna na group of male relatives from one ancestor wey dey help each other for political and social matters. Dem dey settle wahala well well.

questions.q: A student comparing three pre-colonial Nigerian political systems notes that System X had a paramount ruler checked by a council that could demand his suicide, System Y had emirs ruling by Islamic law under a Jihadist-founded caliphate, while System Z had no central ruler but relied on lineage heads, age-grades and oracles. System Z best represents the
o: Oyo Yoruba system
Benin system
Hausa-Fulani system
Igbo system
questions.e: The description of no central ruler, reliance on lineage heads, age-grades and oracles fits the largely acephalous Igbo system. System X refers to Oyo with its Oyo Mesi, while System Y refers to the Hausa-Fulani caliphate structure.
questions.p: System Z wey no get central king but dey use family heads and oracles na Igbo system. Na him be acephalous society.

questions.q: One major function of oracles, such as the Arochukwu oracle, in pre-colonial Igbo political life was to
o: crown new kings in all Igbo towns
serve as a court of final appeal and settle disputes between communities
collect taxes from Igbo villages
command standing armies during inter-village wars
questions.e: In the absence of central political authority, oracles like Arochukwu were consulted to settle disputes and give judgements that communities respected and obeyed. This gave the oracle enormous influence as an informal judicial authority.
questions.p: Because dem no get central king, people dey use oracles like Arochukwu to settle big big village quarrels. Di judgment dey carry weight.

questions.q: Why did the pre-colonial Hausa-Fulani emirates find it easier than the Igbo communities to maintain large, centralized administrative structures?
o: Because Islam provided a unifying religion, law and hierarchy of appointed officials obeying the emir
Because the Hausa-Fulani states had no contact with neighbouring kingdoms
Because the Hausa-Fulani states lacked any form of social stratification
Because the Igbo had no form of government whatsoever
questions.e: Islam gave the Hausa-Fulani states a common religion, legal code (Sharia) and a hierarchy of officials loyal to the emir, which supported large centralized emirates. The Igbo, lacking such unifying religious-political structure, remained organized in smaller autonomous units bound mainly by kinship and oracles.
questions.p: Islam help Hausa-Fulani get one religion, law and order wey make am easy to run big centralized government. Igbo people own different because dem dey use kinship.

questions.q: In British colonial terminology, the term 'Native Authority' referred to which of the following?
o: An association formed by educated elites to oppose colonial rule
A group of missionaries given powers to collect taxes in rural areas
The local ruler or council officially recognised and empowered to exercise authority on behalf of the colonial government
A committee of British district officers who supervised all native courts
questions.e: The Native Authority was the traditional ruler or council legally recognised by the British to perform administrative, judicial and tax functions under Indirect Rule. It was the key local instrument through which colonial policies were implemented.
questions.p: Native Authority na di traditional ruler or council wey British government recognise legally make dem fit help run administration, court matter, and tax collection under Indirect Rule. Na im be di main local tool wey dem take dey do colonial work.

questions.q: In the context of colonial administration, the term 'Warrant Chief' refers to a person who was
o: a missionary appointed by the colonial government to oversee education in a province
a French-trained African administrator posted to rule in Francophone colonies
an individual given a certificate of authority by the British to act as a Native Authority, even without traditional legitimacy
a traditional ruler recognised by the people before colonial rule began
questions.e: Warrant Chiefs were men handed a 'warrant' or certificate by the British to exercise local authority, mostly in areas of Eastern Nigeria that had no centralised chieftaincy. Many lacked genuine traditional legitimacy, which caused resentment among the people.
questions.p: Warrant Chiefs na di people wey British give paper authority to rule, even when dem no get traditional right. E happen mostly for Eastern Nigeria where dem no get king, and dis one come make people vex well well.

questions.q: One major advantage claimed for the British system of Indirect Rule over direct colonial administration was that it
o: allowed the colonial government to govern cheaply by using existing local institutions and personnel
required colonial powers to maintain very large standing armies in every province
completely replaced all traditional customs with European laws and courts
granted full political independence to each colonised territory immediately
questions.e: Indirect Rule was attractive to Britain because it was cost-effective, using chiefs and existing native institutions to govern on behalf of the colonial power. This reduced the number of European officials needed and limited administrative expenses.
questions.p: British like Indirect Rule because e cheap to run. Dem dey use local chiefs and old customs to govern instead of spending plenty money to bring oyinbo officers everywhere.

questions.q: A notable effect of British Indirect Rule on the authority of traditional rulers in Nigeria was that the chiefs
o: became fully independent of colonial control and answered only to their people
lost real power to the people but gained new powers delegated to them by colonial officials, making them more answerable to the British
were abolished entirely and replaced by elected local councils
were given direct representation in the British Parliament in London
questions.e: Under Indirect Rule, chiefs who cooperated were used as agents of the colonial government, collecting taxes and enforcing colonial policies. This made them more accountable to the British administration than to their own subjects, weakening their traditional legitimacy.
questions.p: Indirect Rule make chiefs begin answer to British people instead of dia own citizens. Dem turn to agents wey dey collect tax and enforce oyinbo laws, which come scatter dia real traditional power.

questions.q: A major criticism of French colonial administrative policy regarding chiefs, compared with the British approach, was that French-appointed chiefs were mainly
o: independent monarchs free from any control by French officials
hereditary rulers chosen strictly according to local customary succession
elected by universal adult suffrage among all colonial subjects
agents of the central French administration with little regard for traditional legitimacy, serving mainly to implement French orders
questions.e: Unlike the British who tried to use legitimate traditional rulers, the French often appointed chiefs purely as civil servants loyal to France, regardless of whether they had any traditional right to rule. This made French-appointed chiefs mere agents of central authority rather than true traditional leaders.
questions.p: Unlike British wey try to use traditional rulers, French people just pick anybody as chief make e be like civil servant. Dis chiefs no get traditional legitimacy, na only French orders dem dey obey.

questions.q: The British colonial policy of Indirect Rule, as applied generally across Nigeria, can best be summarised as governing through
o: military governors appointed directly from London with no local involvement
a system of elected African parliaments with full legislative powers
a federation of independent African kingdoms free from British oversight
existing traditional rulers and institutions under the supervision and ultimate authority of British colonial officials
questions.e: Indirect Rule meant that traditional rulers and institutions were retained and used to administer their people, but real authority and final decisions remained with British colonial officials such as Residents and the Governor.
questions.p: Indirect Rule mean say British dey use local traditional rulers to govern di people. But make una know say na British officers still hold di real power and final decision.

questions.q: A key structural difference between the British and French approaches to colonial representation was that, unlike the British colonies, French West African colonies were permitted to
o: maintain completely separate armies from France at all times
elect deputies to sit in the French National Assembly in Paris, at least from certain privileged areas
conduct trade only with Britain and never with France
form their own separate currencies independent of France
questions.e: Under the French policy of Assimilation, residents of privileged areas such as the Four Communes in Senegal could become French citizens and even elect deputies to represent them in the French National Assembly, something the British system of Indirect Rule never allowed for its colonial subjects.
questions.p: For French system, some people for places like Senegal fit vote and send representatives go French parliament for Paris. British system never allow colonies to go sit down for London parliament like dat.

questions.q: The Aborigines' Rights Protection Society (ARPS), formed in the Gold Coast in 1897, is best remembered in West African nationalist history for its success in
o: Preventing the colonial government from alienating communal lands through the Lands Bill
Establishing the first West African university
Securing immediate self-government for the Gold Coast
Organising a region-wide armed uprising against British forces
questions.e: The ARPS mobilised chiefs and educated elite to oppose the Lands Bill, which threatened to transfer communal land ownership to the Crown. This protest forced the colonial government to withdraw the bill. It did not involve armed revolt or create a university.
questions.p: ARPS gather chiefs and educated pipo to fight against di Lands Bill wey wan take our land. Dem succeed to make di colonial government cancel di bill. No be war or university dem start.

questions.q: A key difference between early nationalist organisations in Nigeria before 1930 and the mass-based parties that emerged after 1945 is that the earlier groups mainly
o: Demanded total and immediate independence for Nigeria
Drew their support chiefly from market women and peasant farmers
Consisted of educated elites pressing for limited reforms within colonial rule
Used strikes and boycotts as their main method of protest
questions.e: Before 1930, nationalist activity was led by a small educated elite seeking reforms like more African representation, not outright independence. Mass participation and demands for full self-rule became prominent only after World War II. This shows a progression in nationalist strategy and goals over time.
questions.p: Before 1930, na small educated group dey ask for small-small change for colonial rule. Na after 1945 di real mass movement for full independence start. Dem no bin dey ask for total independence from start.

questions.q: One major contribution of the West African Press to the growth of nationalism in the colonial era was that it
o: Enlightened the people and exposed the weaknesses of colonial administration
Was financed and controlled directly by the colonial government
Trained soldiers for the eventual struggle for independence
Replaced political parties as the main vehicle for self-government
questions.e: Newspapers educated the public, criticised colonial policies, and spread nationalist ideas among the literate population. They were largely owned by nationalists, not the colonial government, and did not train soldiers.
questions.p: Newspapers help to open pipo eye and show say colonial government get fault. Na nationalists get di papers, so dem use am spread ideas for independence. Dem no train soldiers at all.

questions.q: The Action Group, formed in 1951 under the leadership of Chief Obafemi Awolowo, differed from earlier pan-Nigerian nationalist movements mainly because it
o: Began strictly as a labour union before becoming a party
Rejected the use of the regional legislature to pursue its goals
Was founded by northern emirs to unite the three regions
Evolved mainly from a regional cultural body into a political party with a regional support base
questions.e: The Action Group grew out of the Egbe Omo Oduduwa and drew its strongest support from the Western Region. Unlike the NCNC, it had a clearer regional character from the outset. It actively used the regional legislature to advance its programmes.
questions.p: Action Group start from Egbe Omo Oduduwa and e get strong base for Western Region. Dem use regional legislature well-well to push dia agenda. E no be labour union or northern emir group.

questions.q: A major reason the Pan-African Congress movement, especially the 1945 Manchester session, is considered a turning point for West African nationalism is that it
o: Shifted leadership of Pan-Africanism from diaspora elites to African nationalists demanding immediate self-rule
Marked the final defeat of colonial rule in all of Africa
Was organised entirely by the British colonial office
Focused only on economic cooperation among African states
questions.e: The 1945 Manchester Congress was dominated by Africans like Kwame Nkrumah who demanded immediate independence, unlike earlier congresses led mostly by diaspora intellectuals. This radical shift inspired nationalist leaders across West Africa. It was not organised by the colonial office nor focused solely on economics.
questions.p: Di 1945 Manchester meeting change everything because African leaders like Nkrumah start demand independence sharp-sharp. Before, na diaspora pipo dey lead, but now Africans take over. E no be colonial government work.

questions.q: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 is significant in Nigerian nationalist history mainly because it
o: Abolished the regional houses of assembly completely
Granted Nigeria full independence from Britain
Introduced a quasi-federal system and increased African participation in central and regional legislatures
Was accepted by all nationalist leaders without any criticism
questions.e: The Macpherson Constitution introduced regional houses of assembly and gave Nigerians a greater role in government, laying groundwork for federalism. It fell short of independence and was actually criticised for weaknesses like excessive central power. It did not abolish regional houses.
questions.p: Macpherson Constitution bring regional houses and give Nigerians more chance to participate for government. E start di federal system wey we get today. E no give us full independence yet.

questions.q: A common feature shared by early nationalist movements across British West Africa, such as in Nigeria, the Gold Coast, and Sierra Leone, was that they
o: Focused only on local chieftaincy disputes
Were inspired by Western education and used constitutional methods to seek reforms
Relied mainly on armed rebellion to end colonial rule
Received direct military support from the United States
questions.e: Educated elites trained in Western-style schools led most early nationalist movements, favouring petitions, newspapers, and legal channels over violence. There was no US military involvement, and the movements addressed colonial rule broadly, not just chieftaincy matters.
questions.p: Most early nationalist movements for West Africa start from pipo wey go Western school. Dem use newspaper and petition to ask for change instead of fight. No be war or US military help dem.

questions.q: Herbert Macaulay is widely regarded as the father of Nigerian nationalism mainly because he
o: led the Nigerian delegation to the Berlin Conference of 1884
led the Aba Women's Riot of 1929 against colonial taxation
was the first African to be appointed a colonial governor in Nigeria
founded the Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP) in 1923 to contest elective seats created under the Clifford Constitution
questions.e: Herbert Macaulay founded the NNDP in 1923, the first Nigerian political party, to contest the Lagos seats created by the Clifford Constitution. He had no role in the Berlin Conference, was never a governor, and did not lead the Aba Women's Riot.
questions.p: Herbert Macaulay start NNDP for 1923, wey be the very first political party for Naija, make e fit contest elections for Lagos. E no get hand for Berlin Conference, e no be governor, and e no lead Aba Women Riot.

questions.q: A major economic grievance that fuelled nationalist agitation among Nigerian cocoa and palm produce farmers in the 1930s was
o: the abolition of direct taxation on farm produce by the colonial government
the activities of expatriate marketing pools and middlemen who fixed low prices for farmers' produce
the building of railways that reduced farmers' transport costs
the introduction of free primary education which raised taxes
questions.e: European trading firms formed buying pools that kept produce prices artificially low, angering farmers and pushing them to support nationalist causes. The other options describe benefits or non-existent policies, not grievances.
questions.p: Oyibo trading companies join body form buying pools wey dey reduce cocoa and palm oil price anyhow, make farmers vex. Na dis wicked price policy make farmers support nationalists to fight colonial government.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the role of returning World War Two soldiers in strengthening nationalist agitation in Nigeria and West Africa?
o: They formed the first colonial legislative councils in West Africa
They were immediately absorbed into well-paid colonial civil service jobs
They had seen Europeans defeated and humiliated abroad and returned with reduced fear of white superiority, demanding better treatment and political rights
They brought back new farming techniques that reduced rural poverty
questions.e: Ex-servicemen who fought alongside and against Europeans lost their awe of colonial masters and came home unemployed and discontented, becoming vocal nationalists. They were not given good jobs nor did they create legislative councils, which already existed.
questions.p: As World War Two soldiers return, dem see say white man no be god and dem fit die too. Dem come back with ginger to demand political rights and better treatment because dem no fear white man again.

questions.q: In the Gold Coast, the 1948 riots that followed the shooting of ex-servicemen marching peacefully in Accra are mainly remembered for
o: leading to the immediate grant of independence to the Gold Coast
exposing deep colonial economic and political grievances and accelerating constitutional reforms that paved the way for self-government
resulting in the merger of the Gold Coast with Nigeria as one colony
causing the permanent exile of Kwame Nkrumah from the Gold Coast
questions.e: The 1948 Accra riots revealed widespread discontent with colonial rule and pushed Britain to set up the Watson Commission, leading to constitutional changes toward self-government. Independence was not immediate, Nkrumah was not exiled, and the two colonies were never merged.
questions.p: The 1948 Accra riots show say people don tire for colonial rule and force British government to start constitutional reforms. Independence no come sharp sharp, dem no send Nkrumah go exile forever, and dem no merge Gold Coast with Naija.

questions.q: A major role played by educated elites such as lawyers, teachers and doctors in early Nigerian nationalism before 1945 was that they
o: refused all forms of Western education to preserve African culture
organised armed rebellions against colonial garrisons
used petitions, newspapers and legal channels to demand reforms and greater African representation in government
served as colonial governors appointed directly by the British Crown
questions.e: Early educated nationalists relied on peaceful, constitutional methods such as petitions, press campaigns and court cases to press for reforms, rather than armed uprisings. They were themselves products of Western education and never served as colonial governors.
questions.p: Early educated leaders use petition, newspaper, and court case to fight colonial masters peacefully instead of carrying gun. Dem be products of Western education and dem never be colonial governor before.

questions.q: A major reason traditional rulers in some parts of Nigeria were initially cautious or divided in supporting early nationalist movements was that
o: they had no political authority left after the Berlin Conference
they were all forcibly removed from office by the nationalists
colonial law barred traditional rulers from any contact with educated elites
some rulers benefited from the colonial system of indirect rule and feared losing their positions and privileges under a new order
questions.e: Many traditional rulers under indirect rule enjoyed colonial backing, salaries and local power, so some feared that supporting radical nationalism might threaten their privileged position. They were not all removed, and there was no such blanket legal ban on contact with elites.
questions.p: Indirect rule make some traditional rulers enjoy money and power from white man, so dem fear say nationalism go scatter their position. Na why some of them dey fear to support early nationalist movements.

questions.q: The Nigerian Council established in 1914 by Lord Lugard was later replaced by a more representative body under the 1922 Clifford Constitution. What was this new body called?
o: The Legislative Council
The Executive Council
The National Assembly
The House of Chiefs
questions.e: The 1922 Clifford Constitution replaced the Nigerian Council with the Legislative Council, which had law-making powers for the Colony and Southern Provinces. This was a step towards representative government in Nigeria.
questions.p: Na di 1922 Clifford Constitution change di Nigerian Council to Legislative Council wey come dey make law for Colony and Southern Provinces. Dis one na beta step towards representative government for Nigeria.

questions.q: One key weakness of the Clifford Constitution of 1922, often pointed out by Nigerian political thinkers, was that it
o: excluded the Northern Provinces from the legislative arrangements
gave full self-government to all regions at once
transferred all executive powers to elected Nigerians
abolished the office of the Governor completely
questions.e: The Legislative Council created in 1922 only made laws for the Colony and the Southern Provinces, leaving the Northern Provinces under the Governor's direct legislative control. This unequal arrangement was a major criticism of the constitution.
questions.p: Di Legislative Council wey dem create for 1922 only dey make law for Colony and Southern Provinces, while Northern Provinces remain under Governor direct control. Dis unequal arrangement naim pipo take criticize di constitution well well.

questions.q: A notable feature of the Richards Constitution of 1945 was the introduction of the principle of regionalism. Which THREE regions did this constitution formally recognise for deliberative purposes?
o: Northern, Mid-Western and Southern Regions
Eastern, Western and Lagos Regions
Northern, Southern and Colony Regions
Northern, Eastern and Western Regions
questions.e: The Richards Constitution grouped the country into Northern, Eastern and Western Regions, each with its own House of Assembly for deliberation on local matters. This laid the foundation for later regional government in Nigeria.
questions.p: Di Richards Constitution share di country into Northern, Eastern and Western Regions, and each region get dia own House of Assembly to handle local matters. Dis one come set foundation for regional government for Nigeria.

questions.q: Under the Macpherson Constitution of 1951, the central Legislature in Lagos was renamed to reflect a more representative character. What was this renamed body called?
o: The Federal Senate
The Supreme Council
The House of Representatives
The Legislative Council
questions.e: The Macpherson Constitution changed the name of the central legislature from the Legislative Council to the House of Representatives, with members drawn from the three regions. This reflected growing Nigerian participation in central government.
questions.p: Na Macpherson Constitution change di name of di central legislature from Legislative Council to House of Representatives, with members from di three regions. Dis one show say Nigerians dey join hand well well for central government.

questions.q: A major crisis that exposed the weaknesses of the Macpherson Constitution and hastened its review was the
o: Aba women's protest of 1929
1953 Kano riots over the self-government motion
1945 general strike by Nigerian workers
Enugu coal miners' shooting of 1949
questions.e: The 1953 crisis arose when Northern members opposed the motion for self-government in 1956, leading to disturbances in Kano and exposing deep regional disagreements under the Macpherson Constitution. This crisis led to the calling of the 1953 London Conference to review the constitution.
questions.p: Di 1953 crisis happen when Northern members no gree for di motion for self-government for 1956, wey come cause trouble for Kano and show say region pipo no gree for each other. Dis crisis naim make dem call 1953 London Conference.

questions.q: Under the Lyttleton Constitution of 1954, which of the following best describes the new status given to Lagos?
o: It was merged permanently with the Western Region
It became a separate region with its own premier
It was made the Federal Territory under the Federal Government
It became the capital of the Northern Region
questions.e: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 made Lagos a Federal Territory directly administered by the Federal Government, separate from the regions. This arrangement settled disputes over the ownership and control of Lagos among the regions.
questions.p: Di 1954 Lyttleton Constitution make Lagos become Federal Territory wey Federal Government dey direct control, separate from di regions. Dis one settle fight over who own Lagos among di regions.

questions.q: A distinguishing feature of the Lyttleton Constitution of 1954, compared to earlier constitutions, was that it clearly separated powers between the central government and the regions by introducing
o: Exclusive, Concurrent and Residual legislative lists
a complete ban on regional legislatures
a unitary list of government functions only
a single legislative list for all tiers of government
questions.e: The 1954 Lyttleton Constitution divided legislative powers into Exclusive, Concurrent and Residual lists, clarifying which matters belonged to the Federal Government, which were shared, and which were left to the regions. This was a key feature of the federal system it established.
questions.p: Di 1954 Lyttleton Constitution share law-making powers into Exclusive, Concurrent and Residual lists, to show weda na Federal Government or regions suppose handle am. Naim be di main style of di federal system wey dem bring.

questions.q: Before Nigeria's independence in 1960, the Eastern and Western Regions achieved internal self-government in 1957, while the Northern Region attained the same status in a later year because of
o: the absence of any Northern representatives at the constitutional conferences
a decision by the British to punish the North for the 1953 riots
the North's deliberate refusal to join any federal arrangement
the North's fear of domination due to its lower level of Western education and administrative development
questions.e: Northern leaders felt the region was less developed in Western education and administration compared to the South, so they requested more time before taking on self-government, achieving it in 1959. This delay reflected genuine concerns about readiness rather than refusal to participate.
questions.p: Northern leaders feel say dia region never reach South for Western education and administration, so dem ask for more time before self-government, wey dem come get for 1959. Dis delay show say dem just wan ready well well, no be say dem refuse to join.

questions.q: One major reason the Clifford Constitution of 1922 was eventually seen as unsuitable for Nigeria as a whole was that it
o: Granted full internal self-government to all regions at once
Confined elective representation mainly to Lagos and Calabar, leaving most of the country unrepresented
Created a federal system with three autonomous regional legislatures
Abolished the Governor's power to make laws for the colony
questions.e: The Clifford Constitution only allowed a few educated elites in Lagos and Calabar to elect members into the Legislative Council, while the vast majority of Nigerians, especially in the North, had no such representation. This made the constitution unrepresentative of the whole country.
questions.p: Clifford Constitution allow only small group for Lagos and Calabar to vote. E no represent the whole Nigeria well because many people for North no get voice.

questions.q: A key feature of the Macpherson Constitution of 1951 that distinguished it from the Richards Constitution of 1945 was that it
o: Allowed each region to have its own House of Assembly with elected members discussing regional and national issues
Introduced the first Legislative Council for Nigeria
Ended all forms of colonial administration in Nigeria
Provided for a central government over the three regions for the first time
questions.e: Unlike the Richards Constitution, the Macpherson Constitution created Regional Houses of Assembly with elected Nigerian members who debated both regional and national matters, giving Nigerians more say in governance. The Legislative Council and colonial administration already existed earlier.
questions.p: Macpherson Constitution bring Regional Houses of Assembly where Nigerians fit talk matter. E give our people more power to participate pass wetin Richards Constitution do.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why the 1957 Constitutional Conference in London is regarded as a turning point in Nigeria's path to independence?
o: It granted immediate independence to Nigeria without further talks
It agreed on the timetable and conditions that would guide Nigeria towards full self-government
It transferred all legislative powers to the Northern Region alone
It abolished the regional system of government completely
questions.e: At the 1957 conference, Nigerian and British leaders discussed and agreed on the steps, including regional self-government and a future date for independence, that would guide Nigeria's final move to full sovereignty. Independence itself was not declared at that conference.
questions.p: For 1957 conference, leaders agree on how Nigeria go take reach independence. Dem set the plan and conditions for self-government, but dem no declare independence that time.

questions.q: Under the Richards Constitution of 1945, the central Legislative Council was given power to make laws for the whole country, while a new arrangement allowed regional issues to be discussed in
o: Native Authority courts
The Nigerian Council of 1914
Regional Houses of Chiefs only
Three Regional Councils attached to the central legislature
questions.e: The Richards Constitution created Regional Councils for the North, West and East where regional matters could be debated before being forwarded to the central Legislative Council. This was meant to reflect Nigeria's diversity while keeping central control.
questions.p: Richards Constitution create Regional Councils for North, West and East. Na there dem dey discuss regional matter before dem send am go central Legislative Council.

questions.q: A frequent criticism of constitutional development in Nigeria between 1922 and 1951 was that
o: Regional governments were given full control over defence and foreign affairs
Nigerians had no say whatsoever in any council throughout this period
Real power remained firmly in the hands of the Governor and British officials despite the creation of councils
The pace of political change was too fast for Nigerians to adjust to
questions.e: Although Legislative and Regional Councils were created, final decision-making power stayed with the Governor and colonial officials, so Nigerian members mostly had advisory or limited roles. Defence and foreign affairs remained under British control throughout this period.
questions.p: Even as dem create councils, the Governor and British people still get the final say. Nigerian members just dey advise dem, so real power no dey our hand.

questions.q: Which development best illustrates the growth of political parties as a result of constitutional reforms between 1922 and 1951?
o: The creation of a single national party controlled directly by the Governor
The replacement of political parties with traditional rulers' councils
The banning of all political associations by the colonial government
The emergence of parties such as the NCNC, Action Group and NPC to contest elections into the new councils
questions.e: As more Nigerians gained the right to elect representatives into Legislative and Regional Councils, political parties formed to organise candidates and campaign for these seats. This marked a major step in Nigeria's political development towards self-rule.
questions.p: As election start, political parties like NCNC and Action Group come out to contest. This one show say our politics dey grow as we dey move towards self-rule.

questions.q: In the lead up to independence, the principle of a federal system of government, with powers shared between the regions and the centre, was most firmly entrenched by the
o: Lyttleton Constitution of 1954
Nigerian Council of 1914
Clifford Constitution of 1922
Richards Constitution of 1945
questions.e: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 clearly defined and strengthened the federal arrangement by giving each region substantial legislative and executive powers separate from the centre. Earlier constitutions had only introduced limited regionalism without a true federal structure.
questions.p: Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 na im really set the federal system well. E share power between the regions and the centre, unlike the ones wey come before am.

questions.q: A major challenge that delayed the attainment of self-government by the Northern Region, compared to the Eastern and Western Regions, was that
o: The Northern Region rejected the idea of eventual independence for Nigeria
The British government refused to grant self-government to any region before 1960
Northern leaders felt the region needed more time to develop qualified manpower and administrative structures
The North had achieved self-government earlier than the other two regions
questions.e: Northern leaders were cautious about rushing into self-government because they felt the region lagged behind in Western education and trained personnel compared to the South. This led the North to request more time, achieving self-government in 1959 while the East and West did so in 1957.
questions.p: Northern leaders feel say dem no get enough educated people to run government yet. Na why dem ask for more time before dem take self-government for 1959.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the principle of separation of powers as practised under the 1979 and 1999 Nigerian Constitutions?
o: The legislature, executive and judiciary are distinct organs with their own functions and some checks on one another
The President exercises full control over the judiciary without legislative approval
The National Assembly performs both legislative and judicial functions directly
The Head of State combines executive and legislative powers permanently
questions.e: Separation of powers means government functions are divided among three distinct arms that check one another. This was a key feature introduced with the presidential system in 1979 and retained in 1999.
questions.p: Separation of powers mean say dem divide government work into three parts wey dey check each other. Na dis system dem start for 1979 and e still dey inside 1999 Constitution.

questions.q: A key difference between the 1963 Republican Constitution and the 1999 Constitution is that the former operated under which system of government at the centre?
o: Presidential system with an elected executive President
Parliamentary system with a ceremonial President and an executive Prime Minister
Military unitary command structure
Confederal system with autonomous regions
questions.e: The 1963 Constitution retained the parliamentary system inherited from 1960, with a ceremonial President as Head of State and a Prime Minister as Head of Government. The 1999 Constitution instead adopted the presidential system.
questions.p: For 1963, we dey use parliamentary system where Prime Minister be head of government and President just dey for name. But 1999 Constitution change am go presidential system.

questions.q: Under true federalism as practised during the First Republic (1960-1966), the regions enjoyed considerable autonomy mainly because they had separate regional constitutions and could do which of the following?
o: Issue their own national currency
Generate and control significant internal revenue and run their own civil services
Override federal laws on defence and external affairs
Appoint the Federal Prime Minister directly
questions.e: During the First Republic, regions had strong autonomy, including control of substantial internally generated revenue and their own civil services and marketing boards. They could not override federal exclusive matters like defence.
questions.p: During First Republic, regions get power to control their own money and run their civil service. Dem no fit touch federal matter like defence, but dem get enough power to stand on their own.

questions.q: A major reason the 1999 Constitution is often described as having concentrated excessive powers at the federal level, weakening true federalism, is best illustrated by which fact?
o: States are allowed to conduct their own foreign relations independently
Local governments receive allocations directly without federal involvement
States can create their own local police forces without federal approval
The Exclusive Legislative List contains far more items than the Concurrent List, limiting state legislative scope
questions.e: The 1999 Constitution gives the federal government a long Exclusive List covering vital matters, leaving states with a shorter Concurrent List. This imbalance is frequently cited as evidence of over-centralisation compared to true federalism.
questions.p: Exclusive Legislative List get too many items wey only federal government fit handle. Dis one make state government no get enough power to do their own work well.

questions.q: A student researching Nigerian federalism observes that revenue allocation formulas have repeatedly caused disputes between the federal and state governments since 1960. Which factor is the most fundamental underlying cause of this recurring tension?
o: Absence of a national currency before 1973
Lack of any constitutional provision addressing revenue sharing at all
Disagreement over how to fairly share revenue derived mainly from a few resource-producing states, especially oil
Refusal of states to collect any taxes within their territories
questions.e: Revenue allocation disputes mainly stem from disagreements over sharing formulas, particularly because oil revenue is concentrated in a few states while other states depend on federal allocation. This has been a persistent issue across successive constitutions.
questions.p: Wahala about revenue allocation dey happen because states dey fight on how to share oil money. Since oil no dey everywhere, states wey no get oil dey depend on federal allocation.

questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution, which arm of government has the primary responsibility of interpreting the constitution and settling disputes between the federal government and a state government?
o: The Federal Executive Council
The National Assembly
The Independent National Electoral Commission
The Judiciary
questions.e: The judiciary interprets laws and the constitution and resolves disputes, including conflicts between federal and state governments. Courts such as the Supreme Court often settle such intergovernmental disagreements.
questions.p: Na judiciary get power to interpret wetin constitution talk. If federal and state government get fight, na court go settle the matter.

questions.q: A key constitutional safeguard for federalism in Nigeria is that amending certain provisions of the 1999 Constitution requires more than a simple majority in the National Assembly. This requirement is mainly intended to achieve which purpose?
o: Allow the President to amend the constitution without legislative approval
Enable a single region to block all constitutional reviews permanently
Protect the interests of the federating states by requiring broad consensus before major constitutional changes
Ensure only the judiciary can propose constitutional amendments
questions.e: Rigid amendment procedures, often requiring approval by a special majority of the National Assembly and a number of State Houses of Assembly, protect federalism by preventing changes without wide consensus. This guards against one arm or region dominating constitutional reform.
questions.p: To change constitution no be small matter, e need plenty people to agree. Dis one dey protect states so that one person or one region no go just change law anyhow.

questions.q: The countercoup of July 1966, which brought General Yakubu Gowon to power, was primarily motivated by the desire of its planners to:
o: Check the perceived domination of the government by one section of the country
Hand over power immediately to civilian politicians
Prevent the secession of the Eastern Region from Nigeria
Restore the deposed Sardauna of Sokoto to political office
questions.e: The July 1966 countercoup was largely driven by northern officers who felt the January coup had been used to establish domination by one ethnic group, and they sought to correct this imbalance. It was not mainly about Biafra or an immediate civilian handover.
questions.p: Na northern officers do di countercoup sake of say dem feel say one tribe dey control everything. Dem wan balance di power well well, no be say dem wan start war or hand over power sharp sharp.

questions.q: A key economic consequence of prolonged military rule on Nigeria's federalism was the:
o: Strengthening of state governments' control over mineral resources
Gradual weakening of fiscal federalism through centralised revenue allocation
Transfer of taxing powers entirely to local governments
Abolition of the federal account for revenue sharing
questions.e: Military regimes concentrated resource control and revenue allocation at the centre, weakening true fiscal federalism where states had more independent control over resources. The federal account was not abolished, and powers were not shifted to local governments or states as described.
questions.p: Military rule make everything dey center, so states no get enough power to control dia own money. Dis one come weaken how federalism suppose work for Nigeria.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the Supreme Military Council under military rule in Nigeria?
o: A body made up exclusively of state governors
A judicial panel for trying coup plotters
The highest organ combining top military officers for major policy decisions
An advisory council with no binding powers over the Head of State
questions.e: The Supreme Military Council brought together senior military officers as the highest decision-making body during military rule. It was not merely advisory, nor was it composed only of governors or judges.
questions.p: Supreme Military Council na di highest place wey dem dey take big-big decision for military time. Na senior military officers full di place, no be just advisory body.

questions.q: One major argument used to justify prolonged military intervention in Nigerian politics was that the military would:
o: Rule only through state governors without a central command
Abolish the federal structure in favour of a unitary state
Permanently replace the civil service with military officers
Restore discipline and unity before returning power to civilians
questions.e: Military regimes often justified staying in power by claiming the need to restore order, discipline and national unity before eventually handing over to civilians. The other options describe actions not generally claimed as justification for intervention.
questions.p: Military people dey always talk say dem come to fix discipline and bring unity back to di country. Dem dey use dat one justify why dem stay long for power before dem hand over to civilians.

questions.q: A notable feature distinguishing the Murtala Mohammed regime from earlier military administrations was its:
o: Massive and sudden purge of inefficient public officers
Creation of the first set of states in Nigeria
Introduction of a bicameral national assembly
Formation of the first two-party system
questions.e: The Murtala Mohammed regime was known for a sweeping purge of the public service to remove corrupt and inefficient officials, which was unusual in its scale. State creation had occurred earlier under Gowon, and the two-party system came later under Babangida.
questions.p: Murtala Mohammed regime popular well well because e sack plenty lazy and corrupt people for public service. Dat kind massive purge no happen for other military time like dat.

questions.q: Under military rule, the position of the Attorney-General of the Federation was significant mainly because the holder:
o: Automatically became the next Head of State after a coup
Served as the chief law officer advising the military government on legal matters
Controlled the national budget independently of the Head of State
Commanded the armed forces alongside the Head of State
questions.e: The Attorney-General remained the principal legal adviser to government even under military rule, guiding the regime on constitutional and legal issues. The role did not include military command, succession, or independent budget control.
questions.p: Even for military time, Attorney-General still be di person wey dey advise government on wetin law talk. E no get power to command army or control budget.

questions.q: A major reason military regimes in Nigeria found it relatively easy to implement decisions quickly, compared to civilian governments, was that they:
o: Were not subject to debates and approval by an elected legislature
Required judicial approval before issuing any decree
Needed a two-thirds majority vote of a national assembly
Always consulted traditional rulers before taking action
questions.e: Since military governments combined executive and legislative powers and faced no elected parliament to debate or delay policies, decisions could be made and enforced swiftly. The other options describe checks that did not apply to military rule.
questions.p: Military government no get parliament or assembly wey go dey debate wetin dem wan do. Because dem hold executive and legislative power together, dem dey implement decisions very fast.

questions.q: The eventual return to civilian rule in 1999 under General Abdulsalami Abubakar's transition programme was notably different from the Babangista transition in that it:
o: Retained a military President as Head of State after the handover
Cancelled the presidential election results after they were held
Was completed within a relatively short and less protracted timetable
