Involved the creation of more than ten new political parties
questions.e: Abdulsalami Abubakar's transition was comparatively swift, lasting less than a year, unlike the long and troubled Babangida transition that was eventually annulled. Power was fully handed to an elected civilian, and only a few parties were registered, not more than ten.
questions.p: Abdulsalami Abubakar transition no take time like Babangida own wey come end for wahala. E finish di whole process sharp sharp and hand over power to civilian government.

questions.q: During military rule in Nigeria, the body known as the Federal Executive Council (or National Council of Ministers) was mainly responsible for:
o: Serving as the final court of appeal for civil matters
Appointing military governors for the states
Drafting decrees for legislative ratification by state assemblies
Assisting the Head of State in the day-to-day administration of government ministries
questions.e: Under military rule, the Federal Executive Council/National Council of Ministers helped the Head of State run the ministries and implement policy on a daily basis. It did not appoint governors or act as a court; legislative power rested with the Supreme Military Council through decrees, not state assemblies.
questions.p: Under military rule, the Federal Executive Council help Head of State to run ministries and make sure policies work everyday. Dem no dey appoint governors or act as court, na Supreme Military Council dey make laws through decrees.

questions.q: A common method used by military regimes in Nigeria to co-opt experienced civilians into governance without granting them full political power was the appointment of:
o: Elected senators to the Supreme Military Council
Technocrats and retired civil servants as commissioners
Political party chairmen as ministers
Traditional rulers as state governors
questions.e: Military governments often appointed technocrats and experienced retired civil servants as commissioners to benefit from their expertise while keeping ultimate control in military hands. Elected senators and political parties were usually banned under military rule, and traditional rulers were not made governors.
questions.p: Military government dey appoint technocrats and retired civil servants as commissioners make dem help govern while soldier dem still hold the main power. Election and political parties no dey that time, and na only commissioners dem be, not governors.

questions.q: One significant social consequence of prolonged military rule on the Nigerian civil service was that it:
o: Encouraged greater separation between the military and bureaucratic administration
Reduced the civil service entirely to elected local government staff
Strengthened the independence of the civil service from the executive
Militarized the civil service through command-style, top-down directives
questions.e: Military rule introduced a command structure into administration, so civil servants increasingly operated under top-down directives rather than the usual bureaucratic processes of debate and consensus. This reduced, rather than strengthened, civil service independence.
questions.p: Military rule bring command style into government work, meaning civil servants must obey top-down order instead of normal discussion and agreement. This thing make civil service power weak instead of making am strong.

questions.q: Which of the following was a key feature of the state creation exercises carried out by successive military governments in Nigeria?
o: States were created solely based on population census figures
States were created strictly through referenda in each affected region
States were created by decree without recourse to a referendum
States were created only after approval by the National Assembly
questions.e: Military governments created new states through decrees, using their own discretion and advisory panels, without holding referenda or seeking approval from a National Assembly, which did not exist under military rule. This made the process swift but sometimes controversial.
questions.p: Military government dey create new states through decree by using their own power and advisory committees. Dem no dey do referendum or ask National Assembly approval since National Assembly no even dey under military rule.

questions.q: A major argument advanced against the frequent use of military tribunals during military rule in Nigeria was that such tribunals:
o: Often denied accused persons the right of appeal to ordinary courts
Guaranteed the right to trial by jury for accused persons
Were presided over only by senior judges of the Supreme Court
Strictly followed the rules of evidence applied in civil courts
questions.e: Military tribunals were criticized because they often limited or excluded the normal right of appeal to regular courts, unlike the civil court system. They were usually composed of military officers and sometimes judges, but lacked the full safeguards of ordinary judicial process.
questions.p: People dey criticize military tribunals because dem no dey allow accused person to appeal judgment for normal courts. Dem military officers dey run the tribunal and dem no dey follow all the normal court rules.

questions.q: The National Council of State under military administrations in Nigeria mainly served as an advisory body comprising:
o: Trade union leaders and representatives of the organized private sector
The Head of State, former Heads of State, and state governors
Elected senators representing each state of the federation
Only serving military governors and their deputies
questions.e: The National Council of State typically brought together the Head of State, former Heads of State, state governors and some other top office holders to advise on major national issues. It was not composed of senators or trade unions, since elective bodies were suspended under military rule.
questions.p: National Council of State na advisory body where Head of State, former Heads of State, and state governors dey meet to advise government on big national matters. No be senators or trade union members dey inside because military don suspend election.

questions.q: A key reason the transition programme of General Sani Abacha was widely distrusted by Nigerians was that it:
o: Produced five political parties that all eventually endorsed Abacha as sole presidential candidate
Was completed within six months of being announced
Handed over power directly to the Senate President
Allowed only existing political parties from the Second Republic to contest
questions.e: Under Abacha's transition, five registered parties all curiously adopted him as their sole presidential candidate, leading many Nigerians to see the programme as a scheme to transform his military rule into a civilian one. This was unlike earlier transitions which featured competing candidates.
questions.p: Abacha transition program carry five political parties, and all of them come endorse Abacha as the only presidential candidate. This one make many Nigerians believe say military government just wan turn civilian dress wear.

questions.q: One major effect of long periods of military rule on the development of political culture in Nigeria was the:
o: Deepening of grassroots political party structures across the country
Rapid growth of independent, elected legislative institutions
Strengthening of a multi-party system at the local government level
Weakening of the culture of political bargaining, debate and compromise
questions.e: Because military rule relies on command and decree rather than debate, Nigerians had fewer opportunities to practice democratic bargaining and compromise, weakening this aspect of political culture. Political parties and legislatures were largely suspended, so they could not grow during these periods.
questions.p: Because military rule dey use order and decree instead of argument and discussion, Nigerians no get chance to practice how to do political bargaining. This one make political culture weak because parties and parliament no dey function.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the principle of 'local government autonomy' as discussed in Nigerian political studies?
o: The freedom of local councils to print their own currency for local transactions
The ability of a local government to manage its own affairs with minimal interference from the state or federal government
The power of local government chairmen to appoint state commissioners
The right of a local council to declare independence from the state government
questions.e: Local government autonomy means the council can run its affairs, make decisions and manage resources with little outside interference. It does not involve currency, appointing commissioners, or seceding from the state.
questions.p: Local government autonomy mean say council fit run dia own matter and handle dia money with small or no interference from state or federal government. E no mean say dem go print money, appoint commissioner, or break away from state.

questions.q: One major way the traditional (pre-colonial) system of local administration in many Nigerian societies differed from the modern local government system is that traditional administration was mainly based on:
o: Written constitutions approved by a central legislature
Elected councillors voted in through secret ballot
Kinship, age-grades and customary institutions rather than statutory laws
Civil servants transferred from the federal government
questions.e: Pre-colonial administration relied on lineage, age-grades, chieftaincy and custom to maintain order, unlike the modern system which is based on written laws and elections. There were no written constitutions or federal civil servants in that era.
questions.p: Before white man come, our people dey use family lineage, age-grade, and tradition take maintain peace, unlike dis modern time wey we dey use written law and election. Dem no get any written constitution or federal civil servant dat time.

questions.q: A key feature that distinguishes a local government council from a mere administrative agency of the state government in Nigeria is that the council:
o: Possesses a measure of corporate existence with powers to make bye-laws and raise some revenue
Operates strictly on directives from state ministries without any independent powers
Is headed by a civil servant appointed directly by the President
Has no defined area of authority
questions.e: A true local government has corporate status, can make bye-laws, and generate some revenue, marking it as a government rather than a mere agency. An administrative agency would simply carry out directives without such independent powers.
questions.p: Real local government get him own corporate power to make bye-law and collect small money, wey make am different from ordinary government agency. Ordinary agency na just to carry out order without any independent power.

questions.q: During the colonial period, the Native Authority system in Nigeria was primarily used by the British to achieve which of the following?
o: Establishment of a single national government for the whole of West Africa
Administration of the colony through existing traditional rulers under colonial supervision
Immediate transfer of full political power to elected Nigerian politicians
Direct taxation of only foreign companies operating in Nigeria
questions.e: The Native Authority system allowed the British to govern through traditional rulers and chiefs who were supervised by colonial officers, which was cost-effective and convenient. It was not about taxing foreign firms or forming a West African union.
questions.p: Na through Native Authority system British take use our traditional rulers govern the colony under dia supervision because e dey cheap and easy. E no concern tax for foreign company or West African union.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most accurate reason why local government is often regarded as a veritable instrument for grassroots development in Nigeria?
o: It replaces the need for a state government entirely
It is located far away from the people it serves
It controls the national armed forces and foreign policy
It brings government closer to the people and allows direct participation in decisions affecting their immediate community
questions.e: Local government is close to the people, enabling them to participate directly in decisions on roads, markets, health centres and other local needs. It has no role in defence or foreign policy and does not replace state government.
questions.p: Local government dey near people, so e dey make am easy for everybody to join hand decide wetym go help dia community like market and road. E no get business with military work or foreign affairs.

questions.q: Suppose a local government council in a Nigerian state wants to improve its internally generated revenue without depending heavily on statutory allocation. Which of the following measures would best achieve this, based on known local government revenue practices?
o: Waiting for the state House of Assembly to approve a new state creation exercise
Borrowing exclusively from international financial institutions
Strengthening collection of tenement rates, market tolls and motor park levies within its area
Requesting an increase in value-added tax collected by the Federal Inland Revenue Service
questions.e: Tenement rates, market tolls and motor park levies are genuine internal revenue sources that a local council can strengthen through better collection. VAT is a federal matter, foreign borrowing is not a typical local revenue strategy, and state creation is unrelated to revenue generation.
questions.p: If local government wan get more money bymselves, dem suppose tight up how dem dey collect tenement rates, market tolls, and motor park money. VAT na federal matter and foreign loan no be local council work.

questions.q: A notable weakness of the local government system in Nigeria, often linked to poor service delivery, is the frequent practice of state governments:
o: Dissolving elected local government councils and replacing them with caretaker committees for long periods
Increasing the statutory allocation to local governments beyond constitutional provisions
Granting local councils full control over state judiciary appointments
Allowing local governments to create new states
questions.e: Many state governments dissolve democratically elected councils and install caretaker committees, which weakens accountability and continuity in service delivery. The other options describe powers local governments do not have under the Constitution.
questions.p: Plenty state government like to scatter elected local council make dem put caretaker committee, and dis one dey scatter good work and accountability. Local government no get power to create state or touch judiciary.

questions.q: Which of the following best illustrates the relationship between a local government council and traditional rulers in contemporary Nigerian local administration?
o: Traditional rulers automatically become chairmen of local government councils
Traditional rulers often serve in advisory roles, such as through a council of chiefs, supporting the elected local government
Traditional rulers have no recognised role whatsoever in local affairs
Traditional rulers directly control the local government treasury accounts
questions.e: In practice, traditional rulers mostly play advisory and ceremonial roles, often through bodies like a council of chiefs, to support the elected local government administration. They do not automatically hold chairmanship positions or control treasury accounts.
questions.p: Today, traditional rulers dey play advisory role through council of chiefs to help elected local government. Dem no be chairman by force and dem no dey control council money.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the role of the Ward Councillor in a Nigerian local government council?
o: He heads the traditional council of chiefs within the local government area
He is appointed by the state governor to supervise council projects
He represents the interest of his electoral ward and participates in making bye-laws for the council
He serves as the chief accounting officer of the local government treasury
questions.e: Ward Councillors are elected representatives of their wards who sit in the legislative arm of the council and help make bye-laws. They are not appointed by the governor nor in charge of the treasury.
questions.p: Ward Councillor na person wey people for im area elect to represent dem for council. E dey help make bye-laws and e no get anything to do with treasury or governor appointment.

questions.q: A town union in a rural community in Nigeria contributes money and organises communal labour to construct a feeder road linking it to the local government headquarters. This action best illustrates which role of non-governmental bodies in local government administration?
o: Replacing the local government legislative arm in making bye-laws
Acting as a substitute for the local government's constitutional functions
Taking over the revenue collection powers of the council
Serving as a pressure group that supplements government efforts in grassroots development
questions.e: Town unions and similar voluntary associations support and complement government efforts at the grassroots by mobilising community resources for development, rather than replacing official council organs or powers.
questions.p: Town union dey help government do work for grassroots by gathering money and labour. Dem no dey replace government, dem just dey support make development reach ground.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs correctly matches a problem of local government administration in Nigeria with its most likely consequence?
o: Inadequate trained manpower - leading to poor planning and inefficient service delivery
Too many political parties contesting elections - leading to abolition of council elections
Excessive local government autonomy - leading to total independence from state supervision
High internally generated revenue - leading to frequent dissolution of councils by governors
questions.e: A shortage of qualified and trained staff weakens planning, budgeting and project execution, resulting in poor service delivery at the grassroots. The other pairings describe situations that do not realistically occur under the Nigerian system.
questions.p: If local government no get trained people, work no go move well. Planning and service delivery go suffer because dem no get technical know-how.

questions.q: A proposal is made that instead of a single local government chairman and council, each Nigerian local government should be run jointly by two elected principal officers with equal executive powers, in the hope of reducing abuse of office. Which major weakness is this proposal most likely to introduce into local government administration?
o: Automatic increase in internally generated revenue
Elimination of the need for a legislative arm in the council
Possible conflict and delay in decision-making arising from divided executive authority
Faster decision-making due to shared responsibility
questions.e: Having two officers with equal executive powers can easily cause disagreement over who has final authority, slowing down decisions. A single, clearly defined executive head is usually preferred to avoid such conflicts.
questions.p: If two people get equal power for executive, dem go dey fight over who get final say. Dis one go make decision-making slow and cause wahala for administration.

questions.q: Which Nigerian foreign policy institution is charged with providing professional training and research support to diplomats and officials involved in external relations?
o: National Assembly Committee on Foreign Affairs
National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies (NIPSS)
Federal Ministry of Information
Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA)
questions.e: The Nigerian Institute of International Affairs was established to carry out research and training that supports the formulation and conduct of Nigeria's foreign policy. The other bodies listed have different, non-diplomatic specific mandates.
questions.p: Na Nigerian Institute of International Affairs dem set up to dey do research and training for people wey dey handle foreign policy. Na only dis body get dat specific mandate for diplomacy.

questions.q: Nigeria's support for the anti-apartheid struggle in South Africa, including financial contributions to the African National Congress, best illustrates which principle of Nigeria's foreign policy?
o: Strict adherence to non-alignment during the Cold War
Commitment to African unity and decolonisation
Preference for bilateral trade agreements
Pursuit of economic diplomacy
questions.e: Nigeria's backing of anti-apartheid movements shows its deep commitment to the liberation and unity of the African continent. It was not mainly about trade, non-alignment, or economic diplomacy.
questions.p: Nigeria help fight apartheid for South Africa because we want make Africa unite and comot colonialism. E no get anything to do with trade or just non-alignment.

questions.q: A new Nigerian ambassador is to be posted to a foreign country. According to constitutional provisions on foreign policy, whose confirmation is required before the appointment takes full effect?
o: The Council of State
The Nigerian Institute of International Affairs
The Federal Executive Council only
The Senate
questions.e: Under the 1999 Constitution, ambassadorial appointments made by the President require confirmation by the Senate. This is part of the checks placed on the executive in foreign affairs matters.
questions.p: Na Senate must first approve any ambassador wey President wan send abroad before the person fit start work. Dem put dis law make checks dey for executive power.

questions.q: Which of these best explains why Nigeria champions the principle of respect for the territorial integrity of African states in its foreign policy?
o: To discourage secessionist tendencies and promote stability across the continent
To allow stronger states to dominate weaker neighbours
To reduce the number of African Union member states
To justify Nigeria's territorial expansion into neighbouring countries
questions.e: Nigeria upholds territorial integrity to prevent boundary disputes and secessionist conflicts that could destabilise Africa, given its own experience with the civil war. The other options contradict the spirit of this principle.
questions.p: Nigeria dey support make nobody scatter Africa country boundaries because we want stability everywhere. We no want make secessionist wahala or border fight tear Africa apart.

questions.q: A foreign company wishes to invest in Nigeria's solid minerals sector, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs works with the Ministry of Trade to attract this investment through bilateral talks. This activity is best described as an example of which foreign policy instrument?
o: Cultural diplomacy
Economic diplomacy
Shuttle diplomacy
Military diplomacy
questions.e: Using foreign relations to attract investment and promote trade is economic diplomacy. It does not involve military, cultural exchange, or rapid back-and-forth negotiations that define the other terms.
questions.p: When country use foreign relations to find investor and build business, na economic diplomacy be that. E no be military or cultural matter at all.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most significant domestic constraint that has historically limited the effectiveness of Nigeria's foreign policy despite its stated leadership ambitions in Africa?
o: Too many diplomatic missions abroad
Excessive involvement in global sporting competitions
Persistent internal economic and political instability
Overuse of economic diplomacy as a strategy
questions.e: Internal problems such as weak economy, corruption, and political instability reduce the resources and credibility Nigeria needs to project strong leadership abroad. The other options are not genuine structural constraints on foreign policy.
questions.p: Na inside wahala like bad economy and political instability dey reduce Nigeria strength to lead for outside world. E dey make am hard to use full power for foreign policy.

questions.q: A Nigerian foreign policy analyst argues that Nigeria's decisions on international issues should always first consider their effect on fellow African nations before other regions. This argument is best described as support for which concept?
o: Diplomatic isolationism from African affairs
Afrocentrism as the center-piece of Nigeria's foreign policy
Policy of strict neutrality among global powers
Internationalism without regional preference
questions.e: Placing Africa first in foreign policy decisions reflects Afrocentrism, which has guided Nigeria's external relations since independence. The other options describe positions that either ignore or contradict this African-focused priority.
questions.p: When Nigeria put Africa for front for any international matter, na Afrocentrism be that. Na the main way Nigeria don dey run her foreign policy since before.

questions.q: The United Nations was formally established in 1945 mainly to replace an earlier international body that had failed to prevent a major world conflict. Which organisation did the UN essentially succeed?
o: The Berlin Conference
The Congress of Vienna
The League of Nations
The Non-Aligned Movement
questions.e: The United Nations was founded in 1945 to replace the League of Nations, which had collapsed and failed to stop the Second World War. The other options are unrelated historical bodies.
questions.p: Dem form United Nations for 1945 to replace League of Nations wey fail to stop Second World War. Other options no get anything to do with wetin UN replace.

questions.q: A new nation gains independence and wishes to join the United Nations as a full member state. Which organ of the UN must approve the application before it becomes valid?
o: The General Assembly, on recommendation of the Security Council
The Economic and Social Council
The Secretariat alone
The International Court of Justice
questions.e: Admission of new members requires the Security Council to recommend the applicant, after which the General Assembly votes to admit it. The Secretariat and ECOSOC have no power to admit members, and the Court only settles legal disputes.
questions.p: Before country fit join UN, Security Council must recommend am first. After that, General Assembly go come vote to accept the new member.

questions.q: One of the founding objectives of the African Union, as stated in its Constitutive Act, is to accelerate the political and socio-economic integration of the continent. Which of the following best describes another core objective of the AU?
o: To fix the exchange rate of all African currencies
To supervise elections in non-African countries
To grant visas to African citizens travelling to Europe
To defend the sovereignty and territorial integrity of member states
questions.e: The AU's Constitutive Act lists defending the sovereignty, territorial integrity and independence of member states as a core objective. The other options describe functions outside the AU's mandate.
questions.p: AU get aim to protect the sovereignty and land of all member states. Other options no be part of wetin AU dey do at all.

questions.q: ECOWAS was created partly to deepen economic cooperation among West African states through a common market. Which of these is a direct economic objective of ECOWAS?
o: Control of oil prices for non-member states
Appointment of judges to the International Criminal Court
Establishment of a single West African currency and customs union
Supervision of the Commonwealth Games in West Africa
questions.e: ECOWAS aims to promote economic integration, including moves toward a common currency and a customs union among member states. The other options have nothing to do with ECOWAS's economic goals.
questions.p: ECOWAS get plan to make West African countries trade well, like to get one currency and customs union. The other options no be part of their economic work.

questions.q: A country wishing to join the Commonwealth of Nations today need not have been a former British colony, but it must still meet certain shared values. Which of these is a key requirement for Commonwealth membership?
o: Payment of an annual oil quota to member states
Use of the British pound sterling as official currency
Adoption of the British monarch as head of state
Acceptance of democratic principles and respect for human rights
questions.e: Modern Commonwealth membership is based on voluntary association and commitment to shared values such as democracy, human rights and rule of law, not necessarily colonial history or use of British currency. Members may be republics with their own currencies.
questions.p: Commonwealth members must agree to follow democracy and respect human rights. You no need to be British colony or use their money to join.

questions.q: OPEC was formed in 1960 by five oil-producing countries mainly to protect their interests against powerful international oil companies. Which pair below correctly lists two of these five founding members?
o: Angola and Gabon
Iran and Iraq
Norway and Russia
Nigeria and Algeria
questions.e: Iran and Iraq were among the five founding members of OPEC in 1960, alongside Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela. Nigeria and the other listed countries joined OPEC much later.
questions.p: Iran and Iraq na part of the five countries wey start OPEC for 1960. Nigeria and other countries join later for different time.

questions.q: An ECOWAS member state suffers a military coup that overthrows its democratically elected government. Based on established ECOWAS practice in such situations, what action is the organisation most likely to take?
o: Suspend the country from ECOWAS activities and impose sanctions
Transfer the country's oil reserves to OPEC control
Dissolve the African Union in protest
Immediately expel the country from the United Nations
questions.e: ECOWAS has a track record of suspending member states that experience unconstitutional changes of government and imposing sanctions to pressure a return to civilian rule. It has no power over UN membership, oil reserves, or the AU itself.
questions.p: If military take over government for ECOWAS country, dem go suspend the country and put sanctions. Dem no get power to remove country from UN or dissolve AU.

questions.q: The UN Security Council has five permanent members who each hold a special voting power that can block any substantive resolution. What is this power called?
o: Veto power
Proxy power
Quorum power
Mandate power
questions.e: The five permanent members of the Security Council hold veto power, allowing any one of them to block a substantive resolution with a single negative vote. The other terms do not describe this specific Security Council privilege.
questions.p: The five permanent members for Security Council get veto power. If any of dem vote 'no', the resolution no go pass at all.

questions.q: Which of the following is a basic feature of democracy as practised in Nigeria?
o: Control of the economy solely by the state
Periodic free and fair elections
Inheritance of political office by birth
Rule by a single party that cannot be challenged
questions.e: Democracy is government chosen by the people through regular, free and fair elections. The other options describe one-party rule, feudal inheritance, and state-controlled economies, which are not democratic features.
questions.p: Democracy na government wey people choose through election wey dey free and fair. Other options like one-party rule or feudal system no be democracy at all.

questions.q: A key economic feature that distinguishes capitalism from socialism is that under capitalism, the means of production are mainly
o: shared equally among all citizens
owned and controlled by the state
controlled by a council of workers only
owned by private individuals for profit
questions.e: Capitalism is based on private ownership of the means of production, with individuals and firms operating for profit. Socialism, by contrast, emphasises state or collective ownership.
questions.p: Capitalism mean say private people get property and business to make profit. Socialism dey different because na government or everybody dey own property together.

questions.q: In a feudal system such as existed in medieval Europe, land was held by lords who granted portions to vassals mainly in exchange for
o: votes in a national assembly
cash rent paid monthly
loyalty and military service
shares in trading companies
questions.e: Feudalism was based on a hierarchy in which lords granted land (fiefs) to vassals who, in return, pledged loyalty and provided military service. This created a chain of mutual obligation rather than a cash or democratic relationship.
questions.p: For feudal system, lords dey give land to vassals for exchange of loyalty and military help. No be money or vote dem dey use trade for that time.

questions.q: A country's constitution bans all other political parties, places the economy under tight state direction, glorifies an all-powerful leader, and promotes extreme nationalism with strong suppression of dissent. This description best fits
o: liberal democracy
fascism
scientific socialism
classical feudalism
questions.e: Fascism is marked by a single dominant leader, extreme nationalism, suppression of opposition, and state direction of the economy without full state ownership. This combination rules out democracy, socialism, and feudalism, which have different core features.
questions.p: Fascism get one strong leader, extreme nationalism, and dem dey stop people from talk against government. Dis one no be democracy, socialism, or feudalism.

questions.q: Under communism as envisaged by Karl Marx, the ultimate goal of the revolutionary struggle is to establish a society in which
o: private property and social classes disappear completely
political power rotates among competing parties
a hereditary monarchy guides production
multinational companies control all industries
questions.e: Marx saw communism as the final stage of history, where class distinctions and private ownership of property would vanish, leaving a classless, stateless society. The other options describe monarchy, capitalism, and multi-party democracy, which Marx opposed.
questions.p: Karl Marx believe say communism go end class difference and private property. E want society wey no get rich or poor people, just equality for everybody.

questions.q: One major criticism often made against socialism is that it tends to
o: allow private individuals to control all major industries
encourage excessive individual competition for profit
promote inherited titles as the basis of political power
reduce individual initiative because rewards are not tied closely to personal effort
questions.e: Critics argue that because socialism emphasises collective ownership and equal distribution, individuals may have less personal incentive to work hard since rewards are not strictly linked to effort. The other options wrongly describe capitalism or feudalism instead.
questions.p: People wey dey criticize socialism talk say because reward no dey depend on personal effort, people fit no work hard. Dis one dey different from capitalism wey dey encourage competition.

questions.q: A newly independent country adopts a constitution guaranteeing freedom of speech, an independent judiciary, periodic elections open to multiple parties, and a bill of rights protecting citizens from arbitrary arrest. Based on these features, the country can best be described as practising
o: feudal absolutism
totalitarian fascism
constitutional democracy
command communism
questions.e: The combination of free speech, independent courts, multi-party elections, and protected civil rights are defining pillars of constitutional democracy. Fascism suppresses opposition, feudalism rests on land-based hierarchy, and communism typically bans private property and multi-party competition, so these do not fit the description.
questions.p: If country get freedom of speech, independent court, and election with many parties, na constitutional democracy be dat. Other systems like fascism or communism no dey allow all dis freedom.
